articles.title: Gymnastics: GB's Jake Jarman wins historic second silver at World Championships
articles.summary: Jake Jarman becomes the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at the same World Gymnastics Championships as he claims silver in the vault final.
articles.body:
Jake Jarman became the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals in the same World Gymnastics Championships as he claimed silver in the vault final.

Jarman had won silver in the men's floor on Saturday in Rotterdam to become Britain's most decorated athlete in the history of the event.

He achieved a score of 14.650 in the vault final as he finished second behind Armenia's Artur Davtyan, who took gold with 14.850.

"I'm just really happy. The aim is to land on my feet. I know that sounds simple but it really isn't," said 24-year-old Jarman, who has five World Championship medals overall in his career.

"I've had to adapt at these championships, competing all-around and then apparatus alongside the team goals, so I've learnt a lot.

"Today's not quite the score I would be aiming for on vault, but, overall, when I assess where I'm at, it feels like I've managed the competitions really well.

"I've peaked at the right time. I've been really consistent every routine, set some PBs along the way, so it's been a very positive World Championships for me."

British teenager Abigail Martin finished fourth in the women's floor final as she achieved the same score as the bronze medallist but missed out on the tie-break of the execution score.

Martin and France's Maiana Prat both scored 13.466, but the latter had an execution score of 7.866 compared to 18-year-old Martin's 7.666.

Gold went to 17-year-old American Claire Pease.

articles.title: Freelander 8: el todoterreno de lujo que no te sonará a chino
articles.standfirst: La marca de Chery a la que da nombre el antiguo modelo de Land Rover desvela sus primeros datos oficiales, aunque habrá que esperar para conocer las especificaciones europeas
articles.summary: La marca de Chery a la que da nombre el antiguo modelo de Land Rover desvela sus primeros datos oficiales, aunque habrá que esperar para conocer las especificaciones europeas
articles.body: El desembarco de fabricantes asiáticos en Europa no para… aunque sea con una denominación que te sonará a todo menos a chino. Porque una de las siguientes marcas en llegar a nuestro mercado tiene un nombre que reconocerás: Freelander. Se trata de un sello que nace de la colaboración entre Jaguar-Land Rover y el gigante Chery (que ya opera en España con Omoda-Jaecoo y Lepas), que el conglomerado chino utilizará para lanzar en nuestro país uno de los modelos más ambiciosos. Eso sí, el Freelander 8 poco tiene que ver con el SUV compacto de Land Rover más que por su nombre y por su estética, que se inspira en aquel modelo inglés de acceso a la gama a la marca británica. Porque este se va más allá de los cinco metros (5,1) –muy al gusto de los clientes chinos, que quizá se vaya a empezar a imponer también en Europa– y tiene unas aspiraciones mucho mayores: competir con los SUV grandes de lujo. Lo mismo sucede cuando vemos que bajo el capó el Freelander 8 va a adoptar un tren de rodaje híbrido enchufable (la especialidad del gigante asiático) con 620 caballos de potencia. La batería, de 34 kWh, le permitirá superar con holgura los 100 kilómetros en modo eléctrico con cada recarga, aunque la autonomía total se va hasta casi los 900 kilómetros, una cifra destacada para un coche de este tamaño y peso. La marca no ha ofrecido especificaciones técnicas relativas al mercado español, por lo que estas cifras podrán variar cuando este modelo aterrice en nuestro país, ya en 2027. Curiosamente, en la primera información detallada sobre el vehículo no se pone especialmente el acento en sus capacidades para salir fuera del asfalto… aunque teniendo ADN Land Rover, las posee. El Freelander 8 cuenta con el i-ATS (Intelligent All-Terrain System) con configuraciones electrónicas diferentes (hasta 9) dependiendo del escenario de la conducción y el tipo de terreno. Además, cuenta con suspensión neumática y una destacada altura libre al suelo de 26,6 centímetros. En su interior no decepcionará, porque llamará la atención por su enorme pantalla panorámica de 46 pulgadas (1,2 metros de longitud) que funciona como un cuadro de relojes extendido casi a todo lo largo el salpicadero, con una pantalla principal flotante adicional que presume de una resolución en 8K. Se combina, además, con una pantalla para los pasajeros traseros de 17,3 pulgadas. Como es habitual en los fabricantes chinos, se prestará mucha atención a los asientos, que pueden ser de tipo ‘commander’ delante (con una posición más elevada) y los llamados ‘gravedad cero’ en las plazas traseras (asientos con múltiples reglajes, amplia reclinación y todas las funciones de confort –ventilación y masaje–). La tercera fila, según el fabricante, admite también pasajeros adultos. Por su posicionamiento, no extraña que el Freelander 8 pueda ofrecer hasta 30 asistentes de conducción diferentes, si bien el más interesante puede ser el SIVP (Super Intelligent Valet Parking). Este sistema de aparcamiento asistido remoto nos permite bajarnos del vehículo y dejar que sea él el que busque una plaza y estacione, y después acuda a nuestra posición cuando tengamos que reemprender la marcha. Algo que, si funciona bien, se agradecerá porque hablamos de un ‘bicho’ de más de dos metros de ancho… que no cabe en todas las plazas.

articles.title: La inglesa Sivanandan, de 11 años, bate un nuevo registro de precocidad de Judit Polgar
articles.standfirst: Ha logrado el título de maestro internacional masculino
articles.summary: Ha logrado el título de maestro internacional masculino
articles.body: La inglesa Bodhana Sivanandan, de 11 años, sigue batiendo marcas legendarias de la húngara Judit Polgar, la mejor jugadora de la historia, que llegó a ocupar la octava posición en las listas mundiales. Tras conseguir hace menos de un mes ser la gran maestra femenina más joven, ahora, en la localidad montenegrina de Budva, en el Campeonato de Europa de Equipos, ha añadido a su palmarés ser la mujer con menos edad en lograr el título de maestro internacional masculino. Un registro de 1988 pulverizado por la talentosa ajedrecista londinense. Defendiendo el primer tablero del She Plays To Win Lionesses A de Inglaterra, la joven estrella de ajedrez logró su tercer resultado para maestro internacional masculino con 5,5 de 7 posibles, con una actuación (performance) de 2.505, superando en 5 unidades los requisitos que exige las Federación Internacional (FIDE). Sivanandan, pese a comenzar perdiendo con la rusa Aleksandra Goryachkina, número dos mundial, supo mantener la calma y ganó en días posteriores a la india Darshini Sri y a la austriaca Olga Badelka, empató con la experimentada georgiana Nino Batsiashvili y superó a la croata Ena Cvitan, la lituana Arina Budiak y la sueca Viktoria Johansson. Además, Sivanandan fue cuarta en la clasificación del primer tablero, solo superada por Goryachkina, Batsiashvili y la rusa Polina Shuvalova, y pone su nombre en la lista de los 10 jugadores más jóvenes de todos los tiempos en lograr el pergamino de maestro internacional masculino, codeándose con nombres como el del uzbeko Nodirbek Abdusattorov, en la actualidad 5º del mundo, o el argentino Faustino Oro. Sivanandan-Batsiashvili Campeonato de Europa por Equipos Budva, 4ª ronda.

images.caption: La inglesa Bodhana Sivanandan, de 11 años, en primer plano a la derecha. ECU

articles.title: Kaylia Nemour se va del Mundial de Rotterdam con dos oros individuales
articles.standfirst: La argelina se reivindica de su chasco en el concurso completo con un nuevo título en la barra de equilibrio tras vencer el sábado en las barras asimétricas
articles.summary: La argelina se reivindica de su chasco en el concurso completo con un nuevo título en la barra de equilibrio tras vencer el sábado en las barras asimétricas
articles.body: La gimnasta argelina Kaylia Nemour se resarció del tremendo batacazo que sufrió en la final del concurso completo, en la que ni tan siquiera pudo subir al podio pese a partir como la gran favorita al triunfo, tras despedirse de los Mundiales de Rotterdam con un segundo oro al imponerse este domingo en la final de barra de equilibrio. Nemour, que el sábado ya se impuso en la final de las barras asimétricas, hizo valer su perfección en el ejecución para derrotar a la china Qingying Zhang, que defendía el título conquistado el pasado año en los Mundiales de Yakarta. Pero si en la capital de Indonesia Zhang no dio opción a la argelina, a la que aventajó en casi nueve décimas de puntos, en Rotterdam Nemour espoleada por su varapalo en el concurso completo impuso su pulcritud en la ejecución. Poco importó que la china Qingying Zhang presentase un mayor grado de dificultad en su ejercicio, ya que tras lograr una misma nota de 14,566 puntos, Nemour se alzó con la medalla de oro gracias a su mejor ejecución, tras ser valorada por los jueces con 8,266 unidades por las 8,066 que logró la gimnasta asiática. Quien no dio margen a la sorpresa fue el chino Jingyuan Zou, doble campeón olímpico, que confirmó su condición como indiscutible 'rey' de las paralelas, tras conquistar su quinto título de campeón del mundo de la especialidad. Zou, que logró una puntuación de 15,733, aventajó en ocho décimas de punto al croata Illia Kovtun, que se colgó la medalla de plata con una nota de 14,900 puntos, mientras que el ruso Daniel Marinov, completó el podio con una calificación de 14.866 unidades. Tampoco falló el armernio Artur Davtyan que, tras tener que 'conformarse' con la medalla de plata tanto en los Juegos Olímpicos de París como en los Mundiales disputados el pasado año en Yakarta, logró, por fin, subir a lo más alto del podio en la final de salto. Davtyan, que logró una puntuación de 14,850, aventajó en dos décimas de punto al británico Jake Jarman, plata con una nota de 14,650 unidades, y en casi medio punto a Sebastian Sponevik, que hizo historia al convertirse en el primer gimnasta noruego en subir al podio en unos Campeonatos del Mundo. Mucho más lejos quedó el filipino Carlos Yulo, el hombre que privó del oro a Artur Davtyan tanto en los Juegos de París como en los Mundiales de Yakarta, que se vio relegado a la séptima posición con una nota de 13,833, casi un punto menos que el armenio. Completó la nómina de ganadores la estadounidense Claire Pease, que a sus 17 años y en su estreno en un Campeonato del Mundo se proclamó nueva campeona universal de suelo con una nota de 13,866 puntos. Tres décimas de punto más que su compatriota Reese Esponda, que se colgó la plata con 13,566 unidades, mientras que el bronce fue para la francesa Maiana Prat con una calificación de 13,466 puntos.

images.caption: Salida de Kaylia Nemour durante su ejercicio en la barra de equilibrio. LAPRESSE

articles.title: Camilo Durán brilla en Escocia y ya es el máximo goleador
articles.standfirst: Camilo Durán le dio la victoria al Celtic contra el Hibernian en la Liga de Escocia
articles.summary: Camilo Durán le dio la victoria al Celtic contra el Hibernian en la Liga de Escocia
articles.body: El delantero colombiano Camilo Durán sigue demostrando que su adaptación al fútbol europeo ha sido inmejorable. Este domingo, el atacante de 24 años volvió a dejar su sello en la Scottish Premiership al anotar un tanto decisivo en la victoria del Celtic 1-2 frente al Hibernian en condición de visitante, en compromiso correspondiente a la décima jornada del campeonato. El encuentro disputado en el mítico estadio Easter Road no pintaba sencillo para los verdiblancos. El conjunto local se adelantó temprano en el marcador gracias a una anotación de Owen Elding apenas al minuto 3 de la primera parte. Sin embargo, la reacción del Celtic no tardó en gestarse. Antes de que culminara la etapa inicial, un autogol de Jason Kerr al minuto 5 devolvió la paridad transitoria. Y cuando el cronómetro marcaba el minuto 43, apareció toda la jerarquía de Camilo Durán: el delantero nacional aprovechó una jugada ofensiva para sacar un preciso y potente remate que venció la resistencia del arco rival, decretando el 1-2 definitivo que silenció a la afición local. Con este triunfo, los de Glasgow administran con solidez la ventaja en el complemento y se aseguran los tres puntos en una plaza históricamente complicada. Con esta nueva anotación, Durán consolida su gran momento de forma en la liga escocesa, reafirmando su presencia en la parte alta de la tabla de artilleros y ratificando la confianza que le ha depositado el cuerpo técnico del Celtic desde su llegada. Su impresionante rendimiento ofensivo —sumando actuaciones destacadas tanto a nivel local como en competiciones europeas— lo mantiene bajo los focos del balompié internacional y alimenta su ilusión de consolidarse definitivamente en las convocatorias de la Selección Colombia de cara a los próximos retos del combinado nacional. Por lo pronto, el Celtic festeja y duerme en la parte más alta de la clasificación con 27 unidades, impulsado firmemente por los goles y el olfato anotador de un Camilo Durán encendido que pisa con fuerza en el viejo continente.

images.caption: Camilo Durán no para: gol decisivo con el Celtic frente al Hibernian.

articles.title: Jhon Durán se recupera en tiempo récord y su técnico ironiza: de tres meses a tres días
articles.standfirst: Marco Silva ironiza sobre la rápida recuperación de Jhon Durán en el Benfica
articles.summary: Marco Silva ironiza sobre la rápida recuperación de Jhon Durán en el Benfica
articles.body: El delantero colombiano Jhon Durán ha vuelto a encender las buenas noticias en el Benfica. Tras encender las alarmas a mediados de semana por una molestia en la rodilla que lo marginó del duelo de la Europa League ante el Omonia, el atacante nacional protagonizó una recuperación exprés que sorprendió a propios y extraños. El técnico del conjunto portugués, Marco Silva, confirmó la noticia en la previa del partido frente al Santa Clara y, con un toque de ironía y sarcasmo, se refirió al tiempo estimado que la prensa local había pronosticado inicialmente: “Durán viajará con nosotros. Se recuperó rápidamente, de tres meses a tres días, lo cual es fantástico”, expresó el estratega aludiendo a los rumores y especulaciones exageradas sobre la gravedad de la lesión. La lesión de rodilla que sufrió el colombiano generó preocupación debido a que se especulaba con una baja prolongada. Sin embargo, todo quedó en un susto: el artillero necesitó apenas tres días de trabajos diferenciados y evolución médica para ponerse a tope bajo las órdenes del cuerpo técnico. Con esta pronta recuperación, Durán integra la convocatoria del Benfica para visitar este lunes al Santa Clara en el estadio San Miguel, en el marco de la novena jornada de la Liga de Portugal. El timonel aseguró que el atacante "está listo para jugar", por lo que se espera que pueda sumar minutos importantes en busca de tres unidades vitales para los de Lisboa. Antes de este pequeño traspié físico, Jhon Durán se encontraba consolidando su buen momento en el fútbol europeo, habiendo alcanzado su tercera titularidad consecutiva con el cuadro portugués. En lo que va de la temporada, el delantero cafetero acumula un total de 14 partidos disputados y 4 anotaciones, ratificando su importancia en el esquema ofensivo del Benfica, que actualmente marcha en la segunda posición de la liga local (escoltando al Porto) y con la mira puesta también en los cuartos de final de la Copa de la Liga ante el Gil Vicente.

images.caption: Jhon Durán pasa de baja larga a estar listo en tres días.

articles.title: Marino Hinestroza se viste de héroe marcando doblete agónico con Vasco da Gama
articles.standfirst: Marino Hinestroza brilla con doblete en el triunfo de Vasco da Gama sobre Corinthians
articles.summary: Marino Hinestroza brilla con doblete en el triunfo de Vasco da Gama sobre Corinthians
articles.body: El extremo Marino Hinestroza se vistió de héroe en el fútbol brasileño al marcar su primer doblete con la camiseta del Vasco da Gama frente al Corinthians. En un vibrante encuentro disputado en el estadio San Januario por la fecha 31 del Brasileirao, Vasco da Gama recibió a un Corinthians que estrenaba en el banquillo al neerlandés Clarence Seedorf. El partido comenzó adverso para los locales, pero el rumbo dio un giro inesperado al minuto 37 de la primera parte: Carlos Andrés 'Tinito' Gómez sufrió molestias físicas y su lugar fue tomado por Marino Hinestroza. Tras ir abajo en el marcador por 1-2, el exjugador de Atlético Nacional se convirtió en el faro ofensivo del equipo dirigido por Pedro Emanuel. Primero, al minuto 88, capturó un rebote al borde del área para decretar el empate parcial. Cuando parecía que el encuentro terminaba en tablas, Hinestroza comandó un rápido contragolpe en el tiempo de adición, se apoyó en una pared precisa y definió con categoría ante el arquero Hugo Souza para sellar el agónico 3-2 definitivo. "Hace un tiempo dije que iba a darlo todo en este momento... Hoy mi trabajo y mi esfuerzo han dado sus frutos", expresó emocionado el atacante tras conseguir su primer doblete en Brasil. Con esta victoria, el conjunto de Río de Janeiro escaló hasta la posición 13 con 38 unidades, tomando un respiro fundamental en su lucha por alejarse de la zona de descenso.

images.caption: Doblete de Marino Hinestroza con Vasco da Gama ante Corinthians. @VascodaGama

articles.title: Things we learned in Miami Dolphins’ 28-25 win over the N.Y. Jets
articles.summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The Miami Dolphins ventured to MetLife Stadium on Sunday seeking their first win of the season in a game against the New York Jets, a...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The Miami Dolphins ventured to MetLife Stadium on Sunday seeking their first win of the season in a game against the New York Jets, and as it turned out the Jets were just the team the Dolphins needed to face.

Miami defeated New York, 28-25, to get the first win of this rebuild under general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and coach Jeff Hafley.

The Dolphins (1-5) cured a lot of ills against the Jets (2-5) , who they've now beaten in 11 of their past 13 meetings, including five of the past six and the past three consecutive.

Dolphins take first lead of season, score multiple TDs and hold halftime lead

The Dolphins took their first lead of the season as a result of the seven-play, 76-yard touchdown drive to open the game. The payoff came on a 7-yard pass from quarterback Malik Willis to rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas in his first game back from an ankle injury after a three-game absence.

When running back Ollie Gordon II scored on a one-yard run later in the first quarter to give the Dolphins a 14-7 lead it marked the first time Miami scored multiple touchdowns in a game. And after Willis scored on a 2-yard run in the second quarter it gave Miami a 21-7 lead and marked its first halftime lead of the season. — Chris Perkins

Douglas, who had two receptions for 70 yards after missing the previous three games with a right ankle injury, made perhaps the play of the game with his 63-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the fourth quarter that gave the Dolphins a 28-17 lead with 4:44 remaining.

Douglas' ability to separate by using his deceptive speed and length was a welcome addition to the offense. Douglas resumed his role as team's best big-play option on offense.

Tight end Greg Dulcich, who doesn't get much publicity, had a standout game with five receptions for 86 yards. Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. was the game's standout as a receiver with five receptions for 115 yards and one touchdown, becoming the first wide receiver to eclipse the 100-yard mark against Miami this season. But Dulcich was a factor, especially in the first half when he did all of his damage to help Miami take a 14-7 halftime lead.

The Dolphins had two sacks, marking the second game of the season they've recorded a sack and the second game in which they recorded multiple sacks. Edge rusher Malik Herring got a third-quarter sack Sunday, his first of the season, and Miami's fifth of the season. The Dolphins entered the game last in the league with four sacks. The next closest teams had eight sacks.

Edge rusher Chop Robinson, the 2024 first-round pick, recorded a timely red zone sack in the fourth quarter on third and goal from the 3-yard line to force a 33-yard field goal that allowed Miami to hold a 21-17 lead.

Special teams issues addressed, but still exist on some level

There were different players on the kickoff coverage team than from Cincinnati, and special teams coordinator Chris Tabor even rotated personnel on the kickoffs. Among the new faces on the Dolphins' first kickoff were wide receivers Chris Bell & Jared Wayne, center Andrew Meyer and linebacker Shaka Heyward. On the second kickoff the Dolphins utilized safeties Kyle Louis, Julius Wood and Zayne Anderson and running back Kaytron Allen as well as edge rusher Max Llewellyn. In the last couple of games starting safeties Dante Trader Jr. and & Michael Taaffe have played less on special teams while starting strongside linebacker Willie Gay Jr., who didn't play Sunday due to illness, has played more.

On another special teams note, kicker Zane Gonzalez had a touchback on the opening kickoff, something previous kicker Riley Patterson couldn't execute last game. On the down side Pinion had a 37-yard punt to the Dolphins' 27-yard line in the third quarter and rookie Kyle Louis was called for holding on a kickoff return in the third quarter, affecting Jaylen Wright's 25-yard return. But Pinion also had a 54-yard punt.

Penalties declined but issues surface again

Wide receiver Malik Washington and left tackle Patrick Paul had holding calls declined on a three-play, eight-yard second quarter possession that resulted in a 47-yard punt by Bradley Pinion. The Dolphins have had too many penalties committed by seasoned veterans this was another example even though both penalties were declined.

A holding call on rookie cornerback Chris Johnson was accepted on the first play of the Jets' ensuing possession. One play later edge rusher Josh Uche was called for illegal hands to the face. Fortunately for the Dolphins the possession ended in a punt.

Cornerback JuJu Brents was called for holding on a 60-yard reception by Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. in the third quarter but it was declined. Brents was called for pass interference on a Jets two-point attempt that gave them another play, which they converted to pull within 28-25 with 3:24 remaining. Herring had an unsportsmanlike conduct in the fourth quarter from the Dolphins' 1-yard line that didn't result in any yardage.

More TE trouble, this time from a familiar face in Mason Taylor

Jets tight end Mason Taylor, the St. Thomas alum and son of Dolphins Hall of Fame defensive end Jason Taylor, had a pair of touchdowns, one in the first quarter and another in the fourth quarter, to extend the Dolphins' tight end misery. Tight ranging from Las Vegas' Michael Mayer to San Francisco's George Kittle, Kansas City's Travis Kelce, Minnesota's T.J. Hockenson and Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki have all had measures of success against Miami.

Taaffe gets second INT, Dolphins get much-needed TO

Rookie safety Michael Taaffe got his team-leading second interception in the second quarter at the Dolphins' 31-yard line when he stepped in front of a pass intended for tight end Mason Taylor. The Dolphins entered the game with just four turnovers, which ranked 29th in the league.

Malik Willis plays best game of the season

Quarterback Malik Willis was 14 of 21 for 208 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions and a 130.7 passer rating as he played his best game of the season.

Willis showed improvement in judgement and accuracy in his first game after the bye. Things started a bit shaky in early going. Willis' short pass to RB Ollie Gordon was batted down by linebacker Jamie Sherwood in the first quarter. But Willis had an 11-yard rush in the red zone in the first quarter and showed smarts on a first-down scramble in the final two minutes of the second quarter in which he stayed inbounds and started his slide after the first down marker.

In the first half, Willis was 10 of 13 for 128 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions and a sparkling 132.9 passer rating in the first half. On third and eight in the fourth quarter it appeared Willis had Douglas open but he threw high, and the errant pass led to a punt. Still, Willis gathered himself and showed what Sullivan and Hafley saw in him during the past two years in Green Bay.

The run game was strong Sunday. Running back Ollie Gordon II had a career-best 103 yards on a career-best 25 carries rushing to power the offense. Gordon had 14 carries for 58 yards in the first half as the Dolphins rushed for 103 yards on 25 carries. This marks the fifth consecutive game over 100 yards rushing. Gordon rushed for a then-career best 100 yards two games ago and 88 yards last game. Miami rushed for 158 yards on a season-best 38 carries.

Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez had a quiet day Sunday with four tackles. The Jets seemed to always have someone on Rodriguez, who entered the game No. 4 as the league's leading tackler with 57. Rodriguez had three tackles through three quarters.

Now, THAT is something you don't see often

The Dolphins were staring a fourth-quarter tie score in the face from the half-yard line after a Braelon Allen rumble to the 1 and then a foul on Miami's Malik Herring. And, what was the response? Three consecutive tackles for loss. Virtually unheard of. Zach Sieler hauled down tight end Andrew Beck at the 2. Then came a Josh Uche stuff of Allen at the 3. And, finally, there was a Chop Robinson sack for a dozen, forcing the Jets to settle for a field goal, and a 21-17 deficit. — Steve Svekis

Ollie Gordon's incredible October about-face rolls on

For the third game in a row, Gordon exceeded what had been his career best in a game in his first 20 games. In their first 20 outings, the most yards Gordon had run for was 46 yards in Atlanta last year. In his three most recent games: 100 rushing yards in Minnesota on Oct. 4, 88 at home against Cincinnati on Oct. 11 and then the definitive 103 against Gang Green.

It is extremely rare to have the sort of dominant run Dolphins have had over Jets (twice)

The win makes the Dolphins 15-3 against New York since Sept. 25, 2017. Among spans of games in a series of at least 15 games, the 15-3 marks the fifth-most dominant run for the Dolphins. The greatest such stint for Miami is the 20-0 it crushed Buffalo with from 1970-79. Almost as impressive is the 19-1 piled up against the Baltimore/Indianapolis Colts from 1977-87. Next up is a previous run against the Jets, going 14-2 from 1970-77. And then, interestingly, comes the Los Angeles Rams, against whom Miami owns a 13-2 all-time mark.

Jeff Hafley needs to be going for two points from the 1 when up by 10 late

Yes, the Dolphins won. But that was wayyyy too conservative in a risk-free situation. Dangerous stuff. A roughing-the-passer penalty on the Dolphins' final touchdown pushed the two-point try, if chosen, from the 2 to the 1. When you need 1 yard to give yourself a two-touchdown lead with 4:44 left, you must go for the 29-17 advantage. If they miss? The Jets, down 27-23, would kick the PAT to make it 27-24. There was no risk to going for two there. Now, a great rebound to go for it on fourth down, but with a ton more risk attached.

Streak of St. Thomas Aquinas massive damage against Dolphins continued

For the third game in a row, the Dolphins saw a graduate of Fort Lauderdale football-powerhouse high school St. Thomas Aquinas do major damage to the aqua-and-orange in a game, as Mason Taylor, son of Dolphins great Jason Taylor, scored two touchdowns, a two-point conversion and a first-down catch on fourth down. At Minnesota, Dallas Turner has two sacks and a forced fumble, and the next week, the Bengals' Jordan Battle snagged two interceptions. Luckily for Miami, there are no former STA Raiders on the Patriots, Miami's next opponent, as of now.

Jordyn Brooks broke through for multiple minus-yardage plays

The Dolphins' most complete defender somehow came into Game 6 without a tackle for loss, but he broke the ice early and often at MetLife, first with a drag down of Jets tight end Jelani Woods for a loss of 1 yard in the first quarter, and then a minus-3 on a completion to Omar Cooper in the second quarter. For a player with 24 TFLs in his past 31 games as a Dolphin heading in to 2026, it was a welcome return to form.

Dolphins' pass rush thrives for a second consecutive road game

Yes, the Dolphins are still on pace for a club-record-smashing 11 games without a sack (they have four such games in their six overall), but they have buzzed the tower pretty solidly their past two games away from South Florida, with four sacks in Minnesota, and then two more in New Jersey on Sunday with a bunch of other big hits on Geno Smith as he released the ball. For those interested, the most games the Dolphins have ever had in a season without a sack was 60 years ago, in the franchise's inaugural campaign, when they were shut out in half of their 14 games.

On deck: New England Patriots, Hard Rock Stadium, Sunday, 4:25 p.m.

The Dolphins get the Patriots off a 10-day break, and Drake Maye coming off a torrid October where he piled up a 119.0 passer rating to go with 129 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
authors: Chris Perkins, Steve Svekis, South Florida Sun-Sentinel

articles.title: Titans vs. Browns Week 7 Player of the Game: RB Tony Pollard
articles.summary: The Week 7 Player of the Game from the Tennessee Titans win/loss over/to the Cleveland Browns is running back Tony Pollard.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans got off to their best start of the season on their first possession in a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns at Nissan Stadium. The offense gained 65 yards and a touchdown, which was more yards than they have gained in three of their entire first halves this season.

Running back Tony Pollard capped the drive with a 36-yard touchdown run and continued that impressive performance for the rest of the game, making the Titans' player of the game an easy choice.

Pollard enjoys playing against the Browns

After his highest career rushing-yard total in a game against the Cleveland Browns last season (161 yards), Pollard had his best game of this season against the Browns. Pollard finished with 129 rushing yards, 26 receiving yards, and three rushing touchdowns (tied for a career high).

Pollard's first two touchdown runs came in the first quarter, giving the Titans an early 14-0 lead, their largest of any game this season. His final touchdown run came on the game-tying drive from the one-yard line to tie the score at 24 with 58 seconds remaining.

Despite the loss, the Titans should be pleased with the running game finally coming to life. Pollard followed up his career game against the Browns last season with over 100 rushing yards in each of his next two games. Tennessee should hope for the same this season as it tries to turn around its 1-6 start.

articles.title: Aaron Jones limited to eight carries in Week 7
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. rushed eight times for 26 yards in Week 7
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. rushed eight times for 26 yards in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts , while adding a single catch for no gain on his lone target.

Why it Matters: Jones did a good job with Jordan Mason sidelined due to injury for the past month or so. However, Jones had a fumble, which was recovered by the Vikings, but it afforded Mason a few more carries, and he racked up 68 yards with 4.5 yards per tote, to just 3.3 yards per carry for Jones. Mason also had 15 rushing attempts, to just eight for Jones. For now, Jones is still worth hanging onto as a low-end RB3 or flex fantasy option, but know that the usage is about to go way down.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo connect for Giants' 27-21 OT win against Texans
articles.summary: After several weeks of uncertainty in the Giants' QB and RB rooms, J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo powered New York to 27-21 overtime win against the Houston...
articles.body:
After several weeks of uncertainty in the Giants' QB and RB rooms, J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo powered New York to a 27-21 overtime win against the Houston Texans in Week 7.

The Giants improve to 4-2-1 with the win.

Though it took a few plays for the Giants' defense to warm up, the addition of Paulson Adebo and Tyler Nubin seemed to revitalize the secondary after a few very shorthanded weeks. Thanks to three solo tackles from Micah McFadden , New York held the Texans to a field goal in their opening drive. Ka'imi Fairbairn drove a 58-yard kick through the posts for the lead.

The Giants responded quickly, easily grabbing a touchdown behind a fiery start from McCarthy. After opening his first drive as a starter with two tosses to Skattebo, Jamies Winston temporarily replaced McCarthy on the third offensive play of the game for a 3rd-and-short tush push before relinquishing the QB spot to McCarthy once again. He then crept up to 4th and 2 before launching a 42-yard pass toward Malik Nabers , who narrowly avoided Kamari Lassiter for the gain. Tyrone Tracy ran the ball into the end zone from the 2-yard line, and Dominic Zvada delivered the extra point for a 7-3 Giants edge.

Two quick incompletions from C.J. Stroud lead to a Houston punt, giving the Giants possession once again. Despite another 40-plus yard toss from McCarthy — this time a 47-yarder to rookie wideout Malachi Fields down the sideline — two plays with negative yardage, a five-yard penalty, and an incomplete throw to Nabers forced the Giants into a 56-yard field goal attempt, which Zvada missed.

McCarthy finished the first quarter 5-for-6 passing for 96 yards, averaging 16 yards per throw.

The second frame began with a quick 3-and-out for each team. On their second drive, the Texans seemed to have figured out a way around the New York defense, but a false start by Ed Ingram on 4th-and-1 knocked them back five yards to New York's 39. Fairbairn's 57-yard field goal attempt was successful, closing the score gap to 7-6.

McCarthy continued to shine as New York got the ball back, evading pressure by gliding through the pocket to buy time and keeping his eyes downfield for open receivers for an 11-yard pass to Nabers and a 29-yarder to Thomas Fidone , who landed just one yard shy of the end zone for his first NFL catch. Winston took the field once again for a sneak, and Zvada nailed the extra point kick for New York's second seven-point score.

Earlier in the drive, Tracy strung together back-to-back runs worth 5 and 7 yards, respectively, before walking off the field slowly, seemingly nursing his leg.

After holding the Texans to just 82 yards up to the two-minute warning, New York's defense started to lose its footing as the Texans marched 90 yards down the field in just seven plays to even the score. Houston first broke through with a 43-yard connection from Stroud to Tank Dell , who made his first catch in nearly two full seasons after rehabbing a gnarly knee injury he sustained Dec. 21, 2024. A 17-yard catch by Dalton Schultz put Houston on the 6, and a pinpoint TD pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. that flew past McFadden landed them in the end zone. A successful two-point conversion knotted the score at 14.

With just 30 seconds left in the game, the Giants tried to regain their lead, but another missed field goal by Zvada — his fifth failed attempt in his last nine — ended the half.

The third quarter was a slog for both teams. New York got the ball back to start the frame, but when McCarthy followed a six-yard run from Skattebo, a 20-yard pass to Fields, and a two-yard run from Devin Singletary with an interception and a five-yard sack at Houston's 32, the Giants elected to punt instead of going for the 55-yard field goal attempt given Zvada's kicking slump.

Both teams then traded 3-and-outs. The momentum almost picked up on the Texans' second drive of the quarter, when McFadden recovered a Woody Marks fumble forced by Giants DL Bobby Jamison-Travis and ran 44 yards for the touchdown, but a replay revealed that Marks was not down by contact and the play was reversed. On his way down, Marks landed awkwardly on his knee and left the field as the referees determined the outcome of the play. Stroud then threw two more incompletions to end the drive, once again leaving the Giants 30 seconds of the quarter to work with.

This time, New York took full advantage. A fake tush push allowed Skattebo to skirt a distracted Texans defense and rush 19 yards, the Giants' longest run of the day up to that point. A quick 4-yard toss to Darnell Mooney landed New York just outside Houston territory to end the frame.

The Giants slowly chipped away yardage as the fourth quarter got underway, taking eight plays to move up to the Houston 30 before McCarthy dug the team out of a 3rd & 9 with a laser 14-yarder to Fields. He then handed the ball off to Skattebo, who dodged a flurry of Houston attacks and ran 16 yards to put the Giants up once again. Zvada's third successful extra point set the score at 21-14 with 8:55 to play.

New York shut down Houston's next drive in Houston territory, but the Texans retaliated, notching their third sack of the day on an all-out blitz and forcing a punt from the Giants' 14. Starting inside the 50-yard line, the Texans strung together seven-straight gains before a 3-yard TD pass to Xavier Hutchinson and a good extra point attempt evened the score with less than a minute to go. Though they regained possession, the Giants were unable to move down the field quickly enough, sending the game to overtime for their second extra-time appearance of the season.

The Texans opened overtime with the ball. Giants OL Kayvon Thibodeauz nearly ended Houston's run early with the first interception of the game but dropped the catch, resulting in another incomplete for Stroud. A second on the next toss meant Houston was forced to punt.

After their lucky tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5, the Giants were taking no chances this time around. After a nine-yard pass to Nabers to start the drive — bringing the wideout to 111 yards on the day for his fourth-straight 11-yard effort — Skattebo darted up the middle of the field nearly unchallenged for a 42-yard gain before running out of gas. A 30-yard touchdown run from Devin Singletary sealed the deal.

Skattebo's team-leading 17 carries and 124 yards surely solidified his role as the team's starting running back once again, a hopeful start to his redemption arc after having his time severely cut in Week 6.

The 23-year-old quickly settled into his new role, completing 20 of his 28 passes for a total of 252 yards (99.1 percent pass rating). With his two long tosses in the first, he becomes the first Giants QB since Eli Manning in 2011 to complete two 40-plus-yard passes in his first game as the starter.

After a bye next weekend, the Giants will head to Philadelphia to take on the NFC East-rival Eagles Nov. 8. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m.

articles.title: Ravens surrender 35 unanswered points in stunning loss to Bengals
articles.summary: Baltimore squandered a 13-0 halftime lead as Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes and Cincinnati handed the Ravens a 35-13 defeat
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens controlled the first half. In the second half, they watched Cincinnati turn a promising divisional performance into an embarrassing defeat. Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes, and the Bengals scored 35 unanswered points after halftime to beat Baltimore 35-13 on Sunday at M&T Bank Stadium.

The Ravens fell to 4-3 and 0-2 in the AFC North, losing a second consecutive divisional game while being shut out after halftime for the second straight week. Cincinnati improved to 4-2. Tyler Huntley completed 23 of 34 passes for 298 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his third consecutive start with Lamar Jackson sidelined by an ankle injury. Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards, including a 48-yard touchdown that gave Baltimore an early lead.

Those numbers could not overcome the reversal that followed.

Baltimore led 13-0 at halftime after outgaining Cincinnati 258-59 and controlling possession for 22 minutes, 20 seconds. Huntley had already thrown for 215 yards, while Burrow had managed just 43. The Bengals immediately changed the game after the break. Burrow found Mike Gesicki for a 6-yard touchdown, then connected with Tee Higgins for a 13-yard score that put Cincinnati up 14-13.

Baltimore had a chance to respond but failed on fourth-and-two from Cincinnati's 12-yard line early in the fourth quarter when Huntley's pass to Josh Cuevas fell incomplete. The Bengals then drove 88 yards and finished with Samaje Perine's 15-yard touchdown run. Burrow later threw touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase and Drew Sample, completing a five-possession touchdown run.

Higgins finished with six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown. Chase added five receptions for 62 yards and a score. Burrow completed 22 of 30 passes for 292 yards without an interception. Baltimore's offense finished 0-for-3 in the red zone and 0-for-2 on fourth down. Derrick Henry managed 45 yards on 17 carries, and the Ravens committed 10 penalties for 57 yards.

Mike Green recorded one sack, and the defense forced no turnovers.

Injuries added to the frustration. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane exited with a knee injury and was ruled out, with Emery Jones Jr. replacing him. Roquan Smith briefly left with a knee injury before returning. The Ravens finished with a 359-358 advantage in total yardage, a statistical edge that offered little consolation after their complete second-half unraveling.

Baltimore visits Buffalo next Sunday, facing another difficult test as questions mount about its ability to sustain offense, finish tackles, and protect leads.

articles.title: Garrett Wilson directs sideline meltdown at Geno Smith during loss to Dolphins
articles.summary: Wilson only had three targets against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins beat the New York Jets , 28-25, in Week 7. It was the Dolphins' first win of the NFL season and the Jets have now lost five of their last six games. As you could probably guess, it very frustrating afternoon in the Meadowlands.

Fans booed the home team as they left the field at halftime. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. had questions for coach Aaron Glenn after he didn't get the ball on a short drive in the second quarter, but at least Glenn knew who got the ball to start the third.

Things finally boiled over in the fourth quarter when Garrett Wilson was seen shouting at quarterback Geno Smith on the sideline.

Wilson finished the game with two catches for 26 yards. He was targeted three times, the same number as Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Davis. Cooper, Mason Taylor and Braelon Allen all had more targets than Wilson during the game.

The Jets' star receiver has only caught one touchdown in October. Not to mention 211 of his 444 receiving yards this season came in just two games.

If you're not winning, there's just no way to keep a wide receiver happy who isn't getting the ball. Wilson is not getting the ball and the Jets are not winning. Losing at home to the Dolphins feels even worse than usual and this won't be the last sideline outburst we'll see from the team this season if something doesn't change.

articles.title: Fans roasted the Steelers for arriving to Paris game in Peaky Blinders-themed outfits
articles.summary: The famously French Peaky Blinders.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers faced the Saints on Sunday at Paris' Stade de France, so naturally, they arrived to the game dressed as characters from ... a British TV show?

Ahead of the Steelers' eventual win in the NFL's first-ever game played in Paris, Aaron Rodgers led his teammates to the stadium in Peaky Blinders -themed suits and newsboy caps. It may have been an early Halloween costume idea, but the Steelers do host the Browns on Nov. 1. That would have been plenty close enough for pregame costumes instead of this game in Paris.

Even the Steelers' Twitter/X account promoted the decidedly Not French outfit choice.

Fans, of course, had jokes because what was even the point of that decision for pregame fits?

articles.title: Browns beat Titans, 27-24, on last second field goal
articles.summary: The Titans fell to the Browns 27-24 after a last-second field goal, despite a standout performance by Tony Pollard.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans started fast and took an early lead, but they couldn't maintain momentum, and the Cleveland Browns came back to win a hard-fought 27-24 on a field goal as time expired.

Cam Ward and the offense struggled with consistency again, and the team endured another disappointing outing in Nashville, full of missed opportunities and turnovers, none more devastating than missing a golden scoring opportunity with three shots at the one-yard line midway through the first half.

The Titans' defense was also a mixed bag and was torched by splash plays all afternoon. They had chances but again failed to deliver when needed.

Missed opportunities : The Titans couldn't capitalize on several key chances, failing again to score in the red zone and turning the ball over after a big defensive stop. Definitely not complementary football.

Passing game : The Titans' passing attack struggled against the Browns, and it wasn't all on Cam Ward, though accuracy issues remain. The receivers had multiple drops, and Carnell Tate fumbled away a second-half drive. This sounds like a broken record, but it needs to change.

Pass rush: A week after dominating the Indianapolis Colts and forcing Daniel Jones into multiple turnovers, the Titans got nothing going against the Browns, giving Watson way too much time to throw.

Deshawn Watson hit Harold Fannon for a 36-yard completion as time was running out, setting up Andre Szmyt for the game-winner as time expired.

RB Tony Pollard : Pollard had a career day against the Browns in 2025 and continued to succeed in 2026, with his best game of the season. Pollard led the Titans with 25 carries for 129 yards and three touchdowns, plus three receptions for 36 yards.

S Kevin Winston Jr. : Winston returned after missing two games and was a physical presence on the back end, often cleaning up as the Browns torched the cornerbacks with slants. He finished leading the Titans with 13 total tackles.

LB Anthony Hill Jr.: Hill looked more like the player who burst onto the scene in his Week 1 NFL debut. The rookie linebacker finished second with 12 total tackles, and notched his first forced fumble.

The Titans suffered a significant loss when punter Tommy Townsend left the game after injuring his left knee on a second-quarter punt. He was initially listed as questionable to return, but he couldn't, forcing Joey Slye into the emergency punter role. Townsed stayed in the game as a holder on field goals in the second half but didn't punt.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh will meet with reporters on Monday afternoon to wrap up the week and set the stage for Week 8. Select players may be made available after Saleh's press conference.

Tennessee will return to practice on Wednesday ahead of a Week 8 game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. Kickoff is scheduled for Noon CDT.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson limited to 44 yards in Week 7
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had four receptions for a team-high 44 yards on seven targets in Week 7
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson had four receptions for a team-high 44 yards on seven targets in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts .

Why it Matters: The offense was hard to watch on both sides in a 16-10 win by Minnesota. The hope is that Jordan Mason is back for the Vikings, and perhaps the threat of a solid run game with Mason and Aaron Jones will open things up a little for the passing game. Jefferson remains a low-end WR1 in all fantasy leagues, but he needs to get going.

articles.title: Studs and duds from Dolphins' first win of the 2026 season
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins defeated the New York Jets 28-25 at MetLife Stadium. Here were their best and worst performers from the win.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins walked into MetLife Stadium for a Week 7 battle with their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets, on Sunday, and left with a 28-25 win.

This victory was Miami's first of the season and their first under head coach Jeff Hafley, as they got their best offensive performance thus far while the defense could've been better.

As we continue to work through this result, let's hand out some credit and criticism to the Dolphins ' studs and duds from Week 7.

This was Willis' best game with the Dolphins, as he completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns. He also used his legs well, running for an additional 37 yards and another score. Willis needs to be decisive going forward, and if he can do that, this won't be Miami's only win.

There were several missed assignments on Sunday throughout the game, including some 52- and 60-yard hookups between Geno Smith and Omar Cooper Jr. as well as a 41-yard completion to Isaiah Davis that led to a Jets touchdown late in the fourth quarter. On top of those issues, Miami continues to get dominated by tight ends. Mason Taylor, son of Dolphins legend Jason Taylor, caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught the two-point attempt that made it a three-point game late.

When De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL earlier this year, it was clear Miami needed someone to separate themselves in the backfield, and Gordon has done just that. On Sunday, he rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown on 4.1 yards per attempt. He's now up to 339 yards and four touchdowns on 4.7 yards per carry this year, which are career highs in all three stats.

While Gordon has stepped up, Wright hasn't been as good as a runner. With all of the success that Gordon found against the Jets, they shut Wright down, as he finished with just eight yards on six carries. He provides something in the return game when he fields the ball cleanly, but he's been a net negative as a runner this season.

Douglas missed the last three games with an ankle injury before returning against the Jets on Sunday, and he had a great game, catching two of his three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns. The offense can have a different gear when he's on the field, so it's good for him to be back out there.

On National Tight End Day, Dulcich caught five passes for 86 yards, which is arguably his best performance since joining the Dolphins last season.

articles.title: Panthers HC Dave Canales is asked about defensive play-calling after getting run over by Bucs
articles.summary: The banged-up Bucs dialed up 46 rushes to 11 passes, and still beat the Panthers by 30. Dave Canales was asked about his defense after the loss.
articles.body:
All the goodwill defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero earned over the past month or so may have just evaporated.

Nothing worked for the Carolina Panthers throughout Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Their highly-productive offense was halted, their special teams faltered multiple times and the focus—as a whole—seemed to be almost non-existent.

But the defense, which was matched up against a very banged-up offense, took the cake.

With their quarterback needing to wear a glove to protect the dislocated thumb on his throwing hand and their No. 1 wide receiver out, the Buccaneers ran their way to the dominant 30-point victory. Tampa dialed up 46 rushing attempts to just 11 passes, and totaled a whopping 258 yards on the ground.

After the game, head coach Dave Canales was asked if the defensive game plan, considering their opposition's restrictions, lacked in facing the run.

"I liked our calls. We had good run calls to take care of some of that run game," Canales replied. "It just really came down to execution. Came down to guys fitting their gaps, setting their blocks and then containing the running backs.

"They [Tampa Bay] did a good job. Again, I can't take that them away from that—being patient with their runs and trying to find voids. But it is stuff we have to look at. It's stuff that we have to attack and something that we've made great strides in. But we can't have setbacks like this."

Evero and the Carolina defense entered Week 7 in a groove, having bounced back from their nightmarish season opener . From Weeks 2 to 6, the unit ranked second in scoring defense, fifth in yards per play and 10th versus the run.

That group, however, was nowhere to be found this time around.

Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content.

articles.title: Liverpool making massive mistake, must agree deal ASAP
articles.summary: Liverpool have got to agree a deal as soon as possible. Their current plan is a recipe for disaster.Liverpool have some work to do, especially with renewing...
articles.body:
Liverpool have got to agree a deal as soon as possible. Their current plan is a recipe for disaster.

Liverpool have some work to do, especially with renewing contracts at the club. The 'big two' in that regard are unquestionably Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker - two all-time greats still operating at the elite level but with expiring deals.

The pair remain on course to leave Liverpool at the end of the season. The Reds will need to figure out exactly how much money they want to give two veteran players and, of course, whether the players themselves actually want to stay.

Either way, the decisions will be seismic for this team. And they're not even the end of it.

Rio Ngumoha needs a new contract as hype around him continues to grow. He's contracted through 2028 and is in talks over renewing that - extending his time at the club for the foreseeable future.

Liverpool are making what looks like a pretty clear mistake with Alexis Mac Allister . The Argentine's contract runs until 2028 and he made it public at the start of the season that he wasn't in talks over a new one.

That's despite the player wanting a new deal. Liverpool "weren't in a position" to give him one, however, and that came after finding that position for both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai - two players signed at the same time as Mac Allister and who play the same role.

Mac Allister's form has now shone a new light on the situation. He's in the running to be Liverpool's best player let alone best midfielder, such has been his start to the campaign.

Despite that, the Telegraph reports that Liverpool are in 'no rush' to give the Argentine a new deal. This is a mistake.

Mac Allister is busy recapturing his 2024/25 title-winning form - something neither Gravenberch or Szoboszlai are managing. The longer that goes on, the more it's going to convince rivals that he's a player they'd quite like.

That becomes an enormous problem closer to his contract expiry. It both makes it harder to convince Mac Allister to stay and drives up his demands in talks. The kind of double-whammy that Liverpool can entirely avoid if they just negotiate a new deal now.

articles.title: Three takeaways from LSU women's basketball's preseason scrimmage
articles.summary: LSU women's basketball played a preseason scrimmage over the weekend. Here are three takeaways.
articles.body:
LSU women's basketball hosted UNT Dallas on Thursday for its first of two exhibition games ahead of the 2026-27 season. The Tigers delivered a 159-32 thrashing inside the PMAC and offered a first look at their rotation.

As expected, Jada Williams and Mikaylah Williams occupied two of the starting guard spots. MiLaysia Fulwiley also cracked the top five, while Grace Knox and ZaKiyah Johnson made up the front court pairing. Four of the five scored over 20 points on Thursday.

LSU shot a whopping 70% from the field and put nine players in the game. The purple and gold scored the game's first 21 points and led by 29 points at the end of the first quarter. Mulkey started subbing in with under five minutes to play, going with Laila Reynolds and Lola Lampley first.

The Tigers controlled the glass and played well in transition. They outmatched the Trailblazers, who used 14 players on Thursday, in every facet.

Here are three takeaways from LSU's first exhibition game of the 2026-27 campaign.

Fulwiley built a reputation as a spark plug off the bench between her time in LSU and South Carolina. The two-time SEC sixth player of the year honoree cracked the starting lineup on Thursday and showed off her skill set in every area. She notched game highs with 32 points, over 30 minutes played, and a whopping 17 assists to go along with seven steals and six rebounds. She made seven three-pointers.

The senior guard looks primed to earn a consistent starting role in her final season of college basketball. Fulwiley has been challenged to improve her defense and point guard skills since arriving in Baton Rouge. Improvements in both, to go along with her creativity on offense, make her a shoo-in for the starting five.

LSU came away with 36 steals and scored 61 points in transition. The purple and gold flipped 46 UNT Dallas turnovers into 82 points. It dominated despite an ever-changing lineup for the Trailblazers, who constantly made changes to get fresh legs on the court.

Despite facing a lower-level team, the Tigers left no breathing room for the Trailblazers to get any rhythm on offense. Mikaylah Williams came away with a game-high 11 steals while Johnson pulled down a game-high 10 rebounds. LSU got 30 of its 51 boards on the defensive glass, which helped limit UNT Dallas to two second-chance points.

Noa Morro and Anna Minaeva came to Baton Rouge heralded as two of the best international pickups of the offseason. Neither saw the court against the Trailblazers, leaving Johnson and Knox to shoulder most of the front court responsibilities alongside Meghan Yarnevich.

After the contest, Mulkey reiterated that both are dealing with injuries, with Minaeva set to be reevaluated on Monday and Morro still recovering from a September surgery. Their health will be a storyline moving forward as the Tigers are small without six-foot-three Morro and six-foot-five Minaeva.

articles.title: Kevin Stefanski comments on Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski praises Michael Penix, Kendal Daniels after Falcons' win over 49ers
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons defeated the San Francisco 49ers by a final score of 29-20 on Sunday to improve to 3-4 overall. The previously undefeated 49ers got off to a quick 14-3 lead, but the Falcons never seemed rattled. The offense did an outstanding job keeping San Francisco's defense off balance.

When the 49ers had a chance to steal the game late, the Falcons defense shut the door, recording two of four total turnovers in the fourth quarter. Rookie Kendal Daniels intercepted Brock Purdy and then recovered a fumble in the final minutes to seal the win for Atlanta.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski was pleased with what he saw from his team on Sunday.

"Proud of the effort, obviously," Stefanski opened his post-game press conference. "Plus-four in the turnover margin is where it starts. Really good finish there. When you're playing a good team - you know great coaches, great players on that side - you have to be about your business and take care of the rock. We took care of it, we took it away, so that's a great recipe for winning in this league."

When asked about Daniels' clutch play down the stretch just one week after suffering a scary neck injury, Stefanski couldn't say enough about his rookie linebacker.

"That's remarkable, truly," Stefanski said of Daniels' performance. "That's unbelievable to just do that and then to make a play at the end. Man, really proud of that kid."

As for quarterback Michael Penix Jr., Stefanski was equally as impressed. Penix finished 25/34 for 213 yards, three touchdowns and a passer rating of 118.9

"I thought Mike was really good throughout the day. You know, that's a very, very good defense. I mean they're excellent and they don't give up big plays. And we took our shots when we had them, and when we didn't, I thought Mike saw it really well."

Watch Stefanski and Penix's full post-game press conferences, as shared by the team's YouTube channel below.

articles.title: Tom Izzo Benched Two Starters in the Final Tune-Up
articles.summary: Izzo changed his starting five in Michigan State's final tune-up, and it did not go his way. #Spartans
articles.body:
Michigan State lost its final exhibition game, 86-79 to Marquette , on Sunday afternoon at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee. Tom Izzo changed the Michigan State starting lineup after losing to UConn in the previous game.

What Changed in the Michigan State Starting Lineup

The Spartans started Jasiah Jervis and Jesse McCulloch, instead of Cam Ward and Anton Bonke. It was the first career start for Jervis, who had come off the bench in the first two exhibitions. The lineup change also moved Jordan Scott from shooting guard to small forward and Coen Carr from small forward to power forward.

The Good: Jasiah Jervis Keeps His Scoring Going

Guard Jasiah Jervis led the team in scoring with 19 points. Jervis kept his efficient three-point shooting going, shooting four for six from beyond the arc after going two for five from three against UConn. It's the second game in a row that Jervis scored double digits, after he put up 11 off the bench in Storrs. The freshman has looked solid in the exhibitions despite the Spartans struggling to win.

Forward Jordan Scott was everywhere on the floor. He scored 18 points and hit three shots from beyond the arc. He also led the Spartans on defense, with four blocks and three steals. The rest of the team didn't share his rim protection, as they combined for just one other block.

The Bad: Jeremy Fears Jr. Has Turnover Troubles

After guard Jeremy Fears Jr. struggled with four turnovers against UConn, he was even worse against Marquette. He had six turnovers and seven assists, struggling to find a good balance. Fears Jr. also struggled with shooting; he finished with 18 points, but a majority came from free throws. He shot three of eight from the field and missed both of his three-point attempts. Fears Jr. will need to be more efficient in scoring and playmaking if he wants to lead the Spartans to a win.

Forward Coen Carr has yet to show he's improved as a scorer or playmaker. In three exhibition games, Carr has combined for 25 points and six assists. He also didn't make a three, going zero for five from beyond the arc. Carr said the coaching staff asked him to be more aggressive , but he looks like he's taken a step back so far, after averaging 12 points per game last season.

The Intriguing: Anton Bonke Out Of The Main Rotation

Michigan State's biggest question mark going into the season has been its center position. Over the offseason, the Spartans got Charlotte transfer center Anton Bonke, who Izzo started in the first two exhibition games. He started against UConn but played only six minutes, and on Sunday he played just three. Izzo is showing he trusts Jesse McCulloch and freshman center Ethan Taylor in his system. The lack of a reliable center hurt Michigan State's rebounding, as Marquette won the rebound battle, 33-23.

Tom Izzo and the Spartans will have just over a week to figure out what they need to fix before the regular season starts. Michigan State will take on Quinnipiac on Nov. 2 at the Breslin Center to open the season.

articles.title: European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit
articles.summary: Luke Littler suffered a quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajski, extending his wait for his elusive ranked TV title; Ross Smith beat Martin Schindler in the European Championship final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen.

Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw.

Schindler was broken in the next but offered a four-leg burst - including finishes of 116 and 127 - to cut the deficit to 9-7 and threaten a famous comeback, but the next three legs went with throw as Smith closed out victory and the £150,000 first prize.

Victory sees Smith join Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as the only players to win multiple European Championship titles, with his latest success following his World Series of Darts title in September and lifting him to world No 6.

"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there going to that end with Martin - he wouldn't let up, would he!" Smith said. "Full credit to him. To have this trophy in my hands, to win another major - I'm absolutely over the moon and drained, but I'm buzzing!"

Luke Littler was the pre-tournament favourite to claim the only missing ranked major from his glittering CV, only for the world No 1 to suffer a shock quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajaski .

Schindler thrashed Jonny Clayton 10-1 and despatched Ratajaski - who eliminated Littler 11-6 in the previous round - to reach his maiden ranked TV final, with the German missing chances to grab the early lead against Smith.

He wasted multiple opportunities to break in the third leg but responded with a 14-dart hold in the next, levelling the match, before Smith quickly pulled away.

Smith took out an 86 finish to break and kept the German crowd quiet by sweeping all five legs in the next mini session, with Schindler only allowed back in when his opponent squandered five darts at double to open a seven-leg lead.

The pair traded breaks of throw before Schindler followed a 15-dart hold by firing successive ton-plus checkouts, with Smith stuttering over the closing legs before wrapping up victory with his fifth match dart.

"It's a strange one. I really don't think I played great this week," Smith added. "I think a lot of players let me off as well, but sometimes you have to win ugly. I'm proud of doing that because you have got to dig deep. You have to really fight hard and I think I've done that this weekend."

Despite just falling short of a first Premier title, Schindler made history in reaching the European Championship final on home soil and becoming the first German to reach a televised final.

"When I started playing darts ten years ago, I didn't expect anything and now I made a major final," said an emotional Schindler.

"I tried everything to win this one, but fair play to Ross, he played well. I lost but I'm still very happy! I'm going to be in the Grand Slam now. That's probably the best part of it!

articles.title: Ross Smith holds on to beat Martin Schindler in European Championship final
articles.summary: Ross Smith holds off home favourite Martin Schindler to win the European Championship title for a second time, with world champion Luke Littler having been knocked out in the quarter-finals.
articles.body:
Ross Smith held off home favourite Martin Schindler to win the European Championship title for a second time, with world champion Luke Littler having been knocked out in the quarter-finals.

England's Smith reeled off six legs in a row as he took an 8-2 lead in the best-of-21 final against Germany's Schindler in Dortmund.

Schindler got it back to 9-7 before Smith, who won the tournament in 2022, managed to cross the line for an 11-8 victory.

"It's absolutely amazing," Smith, who beat Luke Woodhouse 10-6 and Gerwyn Price 11-7 to get to the final, told ITV.

"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there. He wouldn't let up would he? Full credit to him."

Smith won the World Series of Darts Finals in September and added: "To win another major, not just this year, but just to win another major, I'm absolutely over the moon and drained. I'm buzzing."

Schindler thrashed Jonny Clayton 10-1 before beating Littler's conqueror Krzysztof Ratajski 11-6 to reach the final.

Littler's shock exit came in the final match of the quarter-finals in the afternoon session, with Ratajski beating him 10-6.

"Played well in the lead up to today, but just didn't click for me earlier," wrote Littler, who has yet to win the European Championship, in a social media post.

"Thank you for all the support this weekend. The wait for this one goes on."

articles.title: Charles Leclerc reveals Ferrari breakthrough after United States GP podium
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc believes he has made a breakthrough with his Ferrari driving and is confident of challenging for victory in 2026
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc believes he has "unlocked something" in his driving with Ferrari in recent races and is confident he will have a shot at victory before the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season.

The Monegasque driver finished second in the United States Grand Prix, 13 seconds behind race winner and championship leader Kimi Antonelli, after battling Max Verstappen and Lando Norris .

It followed another second-place in Singapore, and Leclerc said his feeling with the car had improved over the last few race weekends.

"Whether I can convert that into a win is a bit difficult to predict, because it's such fine margins, and it also depends on what the upgrade plans of the others are in upcoming races," Leclerc explained during the post-race press conference.

"But the feeling with the car is getting better and better. These cars are very specific and unique, and I feel like, over the last two or three races, I've unlocked something again in terms of driving, and particularly the set-up with my driving.

"Just both together, we've taken a step forward, and I just feel much more comfortable with the car. So I hope that this will result in a win soon. Whether it's in Singapore or here in Austin, we were quite close, so I'm confident that we'll have a shot at winning a race before the end of the season."

The United States Grand Prix kicked off the penultimate triple-header of the season, and the teams and drivers will now head to Mexico City for the Mexican Grand Prix next weekend.

With five race weekends remaining, assuming the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead as planned, Leclerc sits fifth in the drivers' standings but is still in the fight for second. Mercedes' George Russell currently sits second with 242 points. Lewis Hamilton , Max Verstappen and Leclerc are third, fourth and fifth respectively, with only nine points separating second and fifth.

articles.title: Max Verstappen jokes Red Bull should abandon radios after United States GP struggles
articles.summary: Max Verstappen has suggested an unusual solution to Red Bull's ongoing communication failures after a difficult race in Austin
articles.body:
Max Verstappen has complained about Red Bull's repeated radio issues, calling them "a disaster" and joking that they should start communicating in sign language instead.

The four-time champion finished third behind winner Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc at the United States Grand Prix after what was a frustrating and issue-ridden race. And to make things even more difficult, the Dutchman suffered radio issues that made communication with the pitwall much harder than it should have been.

Asked in the press conference following the race how frustrating it is to have those types of issues for a second time, Verstappen was keen to correct the journalist.

"It's not the second time. It's already, I don't know how many times this year. Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It's probably cheaper as well. It's a disaster. Yeah, it's a disaster. It's really frustrating, to be honest," he said.

Verstappen was not the only Red Bull driver to be affected. Team-mate Isack Hadjar , who finished sixth after dropping from third on the opening lap, said he could not hear his engineers properly and left the pits with the wrong engine setting potentially as a result.

"And then I have poor radio coverage. I can't hear what's happening in the pits. I leave the pits with the wrong map," Hadjar told Sky Sports F1.

Radio was only one of several problems Verstappen listed after the race. He was disappointed with the team's tyre choices, lamented a slow pitstop and highlighted inconsistent behaviour from the power unit, which he said had made it impossible to build a rhythm.

"Too many issues with the power unit, where it was just very inconsistent behaviour around the corners, every lap, every corner, different behaviour. So, you can't build up a rhythm, you can't build any kind of consistency in the car. I had a slow pitstop. So, yeah, too many things today that just didn't go well."

The result ended a run of two consecutive wins for the Red Bull driver, who had won in Sepang and Singapore, and he admitted he had been fortunate to finish on the podium.

"We still managed to get on the podium, maybe a little bit lucky with the VSC at the end, but I'll take it," he said.

It was Verstappen's 10th podium of the season. But with five rounds remaining, he is now totally out of contention for the title. If Mercedes' Antonelli finishes in the top nine in Mexico next weekend, he will be the 2026 Formula 1 world champion.

Red Bull arrived in Austin fighting McLaren for third in the constructors' championship, and Verstappen admitted the team had fallen below its usual standards.

"Normally we're very good at these things, but today we weren't," he ended.
