articles.title: Kyler Murray Sends Clear Message After Leading Vikings Past Colts
articles.summary: The Vikings remain undefeated after another narrow victory, but Kyler Murray made it clear that Minnesota's offense still has plenty to improve. The post Kyl...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings needed a spark from Kyler Murray on Sunday. They got one with his legs.

Murray's 35-yard scramble helped set up the Vikings' only touchdown in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on October 25, keeping Minnesota undefeated at 6-0.

But after delivering one of the biggest plays of the afternoon, Murray made it clear that he isn't necessarily looking to become a more frequent runner.

Asked after the game whether he was eager to find more opportunities to take off, Murray pushed back on the suggestion.

"No. I wouldn't say that. I wouldn't say that at all," Murray said. "If coach calls my number, I'm ready for it. If the play presents itself to allow me to do what I did on the run, then that's what it is. But I'm not … I wouldn't say I'm eager."

It's an interesting position for a quarterback whose mobility has helped an otherwise inconsistent Vikings offense remain undefeated.

Kyler Murray Explains His Approach to Running With the Vikings

Murray's biggest play came early in the fourth quarter, with Minnesota trailing 10-6.

Facing a third down, Murray escaped Indianapolis' pressure and sprinted 35 yards before being brought down near the goal line. On the following play, he connected with tight end T.J. Hockenson for a five-yard touchdown that gave Minnesota its first lead.

According to the Minnesota Star Tribune , it was the longest run by a Vikings quarterback since Joe Webb's 65-yard touchdown against Detroit in 2011.

Murray explained that the Colts were playing man coverage and an opening developed when pressure arrived.

"At that point I saw an opening," Murray said. "Got to get out there and just make a play. That's all I was trying to do."

Still, the former No. 1 overall pick emphasized that he prefers operating from the pocket rather than actively looking for rushing opportunities.

"I'm always trying to stay in the pocket and make a play, throw from the pocket," Murray said. "But if that happens, that happens."

He also acknowledged how much pressure his mobility can place on opposing defenses, particularly when plays break down and Minnesota's receivers have time to get open.

That philosophy is consistent with head coach Kevin O'Connell's previous comments about Murray's athleticism. Following Minnesota's October 11 win over New Orleans, O'Connell explained that the team wanted to take advantage of Murray's mobility without prescribing exactly when he should run.

Against Indianapolis, that flexibility produced the Vikings' most important offensive sequence.

Kyler Murray Acknowledges Vikings' Offensive Struggles

Despite the victory, Minnesota's offense had another difficult afternoon.

Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and one touchdown. Justin Jefferson finished with four receptions for 44 yards, while the Vikings managed just one touchdown across the entire game.

Minnesota also converted only three of 11 third-down opportunities and scored a touchdown on one of its two red-zone possessions.

Afterward, Murray expressed confidence in the offense but acknowledged its inability to finish drives.

"We got to put the ball in the end zone," Murray said. "At the end of the day, that's what it comes down to."

Murray agreed with O'Connell's assessment that the offense was getting closer to reaching its potential.

"My confidence will never waver in the group that we have," he said.

For now, the defense continues to provide Minnesota with a substantial margin for error.

The Vikings held Indianapolis scoreless in the second half, and Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones late in the fourth quarter to secure the victory.

"Nothing that they do surprises me," he said of Minnesota's defense. "It's a really special group over there."

Minnesota will face a tougher test of its offensive progress in Week 8 against the Detroit Lions . The Vikings have continued finding ways to win, but Sunday's performance offered another reminder that Murray and the offense still have work ahead.

articles.title: 49ers’ Brock Purdy explains brutal blunder that cost San Francisco during Falcons upset
articles.summary: Coach Kyle Shanahan, QB Brock Purdy and other familiar faces led the 49ers into gridiron battle against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 action that included a...
articles.body:
Coach Kyle Shanahan, QB Brock Purdy and other familiar faces led the 49ers into gridiron battle against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 action that included a Christian McCaffrey injury scare . Fans debated whether San Francisco could finish the season undefeated like the 1972 Miami Dolphins ahead of the game and got their answer as Atlanta won 29-20 during a day when Purdy was intercepted twice.

One interception came when Jessie Bates dove near the sideline and snagged Purdy's pass, which fans thought he intended to throw out-of-bounds. Purdy explained after the game that he was trying to find a 49ers receiver who wasn't where he placed it.

"Yeah, I thought maybe Christian Kirk on the scramble was gonna be there, but towards the end of the throw, as I was going to throw I was like, no it's not, and sort of went to just throw it away by the sideline, and then Bates all of a sudden came across and made a play, and I was like, you gotta be kidding me.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"So in that moment, man, I gotta completely throw the ball away if I'm not gonna make an attempt to a receiver, so," Purdy added.

The day began with news of the 49ers' potential trade interest in Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , who once played in San Francisco. The 49ers' defense held Bijan Robinson, the Falcons' star running back, to just 63 yards on the day while QB Michael Penix Jr. had 213 yards and made them count with three passing touchdowns.

Now 6-1, Shanahan, Purdy and the rest of the 49ers are scheduled to face the Raiders at home on November 8 after a bye week, giving them time to recoup and reassess for what figures to be a grueling midseason run.

articles.title: Video Shows SEC Player in Apparent Altercation as South Carolina Fans Flood the Field
articles.summary: An unforgettable SEC clash ended in total postgame pandemonium at Williams-Brice Stadium after a dramatic 27–24 upset by South Carolina over No. 11 Tennessee...
articles.body:
An unforgettable SEC clash ended in total postgame pandemonium at Williams-Brice Stadium after a dramatic 27–24 upset by South Carolina over No. 11 Tennessee instantly transformed into a chaotic, headline-grabbing scene on the field.

As thousands of overjoyed Gamecock supporters swarmed the playing surface in the immediate aftermath of a walk-off field goal, the sudden influx created bottlenecked exits and safety risks for the visiting team.

South Carolina secured a dramatic 27–24 upset victory over No. 11 Tennessee at Williams-Brice Stadium, clinched by kicker Malik Orsan's walk-off 48-yard field goal. As the ball split the uprights, thousands of Gamecock supporters immediately poured over the walls and swarmed the playing surface to celebrate the signature conference win.

As Tennessee personnel navigated the postgame congestion, video clips circulated on social media highlighting two distinct physical altercations involving Volunteers players.

A seven-second video clip captured an individual holding a mobile device or camera close to the exiting Tennessee players while waving directly in their faces. As the crowd moved around the team, senior defensive lineman Daevin Hobbs was captured walking through the frame carrying a small rod or object in his left hand. Hobbs lowered his right shoulder into the spectator, knocking the fan flat onto the turf before continuing toward the locker room tunnel.

A secondary video clip filmed near the field exit pathway captured a physical exchange between opposing players. Senior linebacker Jeremiah Telander was filmed advancing through the crowd toward South Carolina freshman defensive back Triston Lewis. Telander threw a right-handed swing aimed at Lewis.

The postgame chaos also drew renewed attention to SEC field-storming regulations, with the conference facing heavy standard fines for the massive influx of spectators onto the playing field.

The primary party facing financial penalties is the University of South Carolina. South Carolina allowed thousands of fans to breach security barriers and storm the playing surface at Williams-Brice Stadium immediately following Malik Orsan's walk-off 48-yard field goal. Under Southeastern Conference access-to-competition-area policy, any unauthorized field or court rush results in a flat $500,000 fine. The fine is paid directly to the opposing institution, the University of Tennessee.

While the university itself bears the administrative fine for the field rush, individual disciplinary actions and potential league penalties could follow the physical altercations caught on camera.

The SEC office and Tennessee athletic administration review postgame tape following physical incidents involving fans or opposing players. Depending on their findings regarding defensive lineman Daevin Hobbs and linebacker Jeremiah Telander, individual players could face conference suspensions, internal team discipline, or institutional fines.

articles.title: Seahawks’ Kenneth Walker Decision Draws ‘Punch Himself’ Criticism Ahead of Chiefs Matchup
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks enter Sunday night still stinging from a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Oct. 15, where Sam Darnold was sacked five times a...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks enter Sunday night still stinging from a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Oct. 15, where Sam Darnold was sacked five times and the offense managed just three points on its first eight drives.

Now the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs are coming to town, and amid the Seahawks' growing running back crisis, general manager John Schneider is facing sharp criticism over one offseason call.

Richie Incognito Calls out John Schneider over Kenneth Walker exit

Former NFL offensive lineman Richie Incognito did not hold back on his Initial Contact podcast. He pointed straight at Seattle's rushing attack and the man who built it.

"..I think the biggest factor for Seattle is they have absolutely no run game," Richie Incognito said. "They got the Chiefs coming into their house, and they can look across that sideline at the Super Bowl MVP and John Schneider, the GM of the Seattle Seahawks, should punch himself in the n*** for not even making an offer for this guy."

Incognito also recalled Schneider's parade joke about Walker's contract talks.

"I was watching a video clip of the Super Bowl speech after last season and Schneider saying, 'Oh, Walker was trying to negotiate with me behind the scenes.' John Schneider needs a swift kick to the n*** for letting that guy out the building. Didn't make an offer," Incognito continue.

He also criticized Schneider for passing on the franchise tag and letting Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III walk.

Walker piled up 313 rushing yards and four touchdowns in last year's playoffs. The Athletic reported that Seattle did not make him an offer before free agency opened. Kansas City then signed him to a three-year deal that includes $28.7 million guaranteed.

The move has paid off quickly. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, despite the Chiefs' bye week. His unbeaten start with Kansas City Chiefs has made the criticism louder.

Seattle, meanwhile, has just 643 rushing yards as a team over six games. That works out to about 107 yards per game, and Walker has already topped that total by himself.

Schneider's own comments about the running back position are now being tested.

Schneider's running back plan faces fresh scrutiny

Back in March, Schneider was not worried about a hole at running back.

"That's a position that you can find guys," he told reporters.

Seattle then used the 32nd overall pick in April on Notre Dame running back Jadarian Price. That plan has run into trouble.

Price landed on injured reserve in early October with a chest injury, and Zach Charbonnet is still working back from a torn ACL. With Price sidelined, Emanuel Wilson led Seattle with just 52 rushing yards against Denver.

The Seahawks have kept reshuffling the roster, including a decision to move on from Trevon Diggs and a deadline-day move to activate an offensive weapon. Still, its search for a Walker replacement remains unresolved.

That puts more pressure on the defense, which has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in more than 30 straight games, a streak Walker could test.

The Seahawks sit at 3-3 and need a statement win in primetime. The Chiefs arrive at 5-0 with Walker back in Seattle. Kickoff at Lumen Field is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, and Schneider's biggest offseason call will be on full display.

articles.title: Hamilton Reveals Friday Data Deficit Behind Ferrari Teammate Leclerc’s US GP Podium
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton reveals what he lacked when compared to Charles Leclerc to lose out at the F1 US GP, where a front wing adjustment cost him hugely. Ferrari’s...
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton reveals what he lacked when compared to Charles Leclerc to lose out at the F1 US GP, where a front wing adjustment cost him hugely.

Ferrari 's Hamilton ended up fourth in the F1 US GP at the Circuit of the Americas, just about a second off the podium from Red Bull's Max Verstappen . Teammate Charles Leclerc was second, and the Brit knows the difference that made it happen.

It goes back to Friday when Hamilton started the F1 US GP weekend on the wrong foot and lost valuable time in FP1 and also FP2. It allowed Leclerc to accumulate the data and learning that ultimately made the difference on Sunday.

Hamilton Understood his F1 US GP Problems From Get Go

Hamilton complained that he couldn't turn the car, which is where he started to lose time. "I was lacking pace in the first two stints basically," he said to the media after the F1 US GP. "I just couldn't turn the car. And I think ultimately it all kind of started on Friday. Wrong setup, really, for FP1 and then went the wrong direction in FP2.

"Reverted back and got to a better place for FP3. But there's a subtle difference between Charles and our car, basically just in the race, and it's mostly just to do with the flap for how much wing you put on, and I think we've just been under-hitting it. Continuously under-hitting it for some reason.

"And when you do the lap to the grid, it feels like the car is good and then as soon as the race starts, massive washout and understeer, and I couldn't do anything about it, so they just pulled away. I lost those eight seconds, and that's really why I didn't get that position in the end," summed up Hamilton .

Hamilton Explains How He Got it Sorted at the Pit Stops

How did he manage to have a better end? It was said on the radio. Hamilton wanted to adjust the front wing flap, which is what Ferrari did in the two pit stops. But he was still short by the end of it. That ultimately led to his downer, as he did not have the experience that Leclerc managed to gain in practice.

"Because through the pit stops, I added four clicks," said Hamilton. "Next, at the next pit stop, I added another four clicks, and even then, I'm still another four clicks too short. And it's crazy to be 12 clicks down; we really need to look at how we get to that point. But I think it would have been a bit different if we had started with it, I think, in FP2, where you did in the long run.

"That's where Charles got the experience in that setup, and I didn't get the long run on it, so instead of being on the back foot, but with lots of positives to take, the team seemed to do a really great job with pit stops and strategy, and we obviously had a decent pace today, particularly last stint.

"If I had that in the first two, it would have for sure been in the for sure, been on the podium, I think in the end," summed up Hamilton, who felt the tire strategy went wrong on his end once again. It was not the strategy in itself but the choice of compound. Ultimately, the hard tire was the best of the lot.

Hamilton Felt Hard Tyre was the Best Compound

He had saved two sets of medium tires, which didn't work as well as expected. He thought he made a good start to pounce on ailing Verstappen, but starting on the used soft tire cost him better pace. "Yeah, I mean, I chose to have two medium tires because they didn't think the hard tire was going to be any good," continued Hamilton.

"In hindsight, it would have been two hard tires, which would have been the better one. The hard tire was the best tire. And then it meant I started on a used soft, which is from used to new; it's two seconds of race time. And so, it affects the start as well compared to others that are on the new.

"All the cars ahead are on the new, but I had a really good start, nearly got to third place or whatever it was, but Charles was on the outside, and I didn't get to capitalize on that. But yeah, otherwise, as I said, there are lots of positives to take from it. I think lots of learning.

"I think if, for the next races, I can really get on top of this balance issue that I have, I think we can get much better results. If I had the balance that I need, even if I just had the balancing of the last stint, I would have been right in the fight all the way to the end, but I think even then, another step from there, I think we could have probably qualified better. And so, some good points."

VSC Cost a Podium Chance But Issue was First Two Stints

As pointed out earlier, Hamilton managed to gain massively on the last stint on the hard compound. He got through Lando Norris and had Verstappen in his sights. But a late Virtual Safety Car period potentially cost him laps and time. Ultimately, the first two stints cost him that extra time, which was the difference he had to make.

"I think, well, we have got to have a little bit of a battle with Max in the last couple of laps, so, yeah, that would have been awesome," said Hamilton. "But as I said, I think it was all the first two stints; I just lost so much ground. Can't be giving up that time in the future. I think I really feel like I'm happy with how I drove.

"It took two whole stints to try and get this car to turn, and then once it started to turn in the third stint, I was back on pace with the guys ahead and had a big gap to close — eight or nine seconds or whatever it was — to the car ahead. So those guys are obviously very quick, so I just got to work on not losing that second points," summed up Hamilton.

articles.title: ‘Edgy’ Arch Manning is a better leader, but still mistake-prone
articles.summary: A more fiery attitude and less hesitancy helped the Texas quarterback will his team to victory.
articles.body:
AUSTIN — Does Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian want to see senior quarterback Arch Manning make his "edgy" personality more permanent?

"Yeah, love it," Sarkisian responded. "That fires me up."

Similar to Manning's wild vascillation between high-level plays and confounding errors and turn downs , Manning's personality also swings, from quiet and withdrawn to swaggy and fiery as his confidence ebbs and flows.

On Saturday, Texas got the edgy version in a 34-27 victory over Ole Miss in the wake of back-to-back losses to unranked opponents that saw Manning commit late, game-changing turnovers in both games after week-long speculation swirled about the possibility of Sarkisian taking the rare step of benching his starter .

Sarkisian met personally with Manning last Sunday to challenge his highly-touted quarterback. During the week, Manning's edgy personality emerged. Or re-emerged, depending on the perspective .

"He's edgy right now, and honestly, I appreciate that about him," Sarkisian said Thursday. "At some point, he's got to fight back, and the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates, so I'm looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night."

Over recent weeks, Texas has struggled to translate how players practice into how players play , but Manning did at least take the edginess with which he operated during the week into the Ole Miss game, elevated by his first two rushing touchdowns of the season.

The first, a two-yard run at the end of the first quarter, not only gave the Longhorns a seven-point lead, it also provided an indelible image of Manning's celebration synced perfectly to the heightened experience at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium.

A sideline shot captured the type of fire that has defined the best moments of Manning's Texas tenure. In his worst moments, the absence of it has left a tangible void.

Quantifying the points added or lost by the difference in Manning's leadership is impossible, but the result on Saturday compared to the results the previous two weeks affords some data points, at least.

In between the whistles, the Arch Manning Experience hit some all-too-familiar beats while showing some signs of progress.

The combination of Sarkisian calling more routes over the middle, where Manning is hyper efficient, and the Texas quarterback operating with less hesitancy, an issue that contributed to multiple sacks in last week's loss to Florida, helped the Longhorns race out to a 24-3 lead at halftime on 13-of-19 passing for 171 yards, including a beautiful 50-yard touchdown pass to junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo.

The throw to Wingo was the weekly pinnacle for Manning.

Other decisions ended poorly when Manning admittedly didn't see the defenders who intercepted two of his passes, but at least happened with less hesitancy?

The first came on the type of out route to junior wide receiver Emmett Mosley that Manning missed consistently against the Gators. On the second Texas drive, Ole Miss busted its coverage, leaving two defenders on Mosley as junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo came open on a corner route.

The second interception was more confounding when Manning threw into triple coverage trying to target sophomore tight end Emaree Winston deep down the field.

Of Winston's six receptions this season, only one has come more than 10 yards down the field.

Manning's inability to layer a pass to Winston in another instance is reflective of his regular misfires, albeit one made more difficult by having to reset his feet after moving out of the pocket and throwing across the field.

Manning's other turnover, the sack-fumble on the first drive of the third quarter, wasn't primarily his fault because backup left tackle Andre Cojoe got beat badly on a speed rush.

After another game of highs and lows, Manning and the Longhorns broke their losing streak, and the embattled quarterback shared an emotional moment on the field with his family.

Meeting with the media after the game, Manning provided some further insight into why that moment was so important to him.

"Probably because it was a hard Sunday and I went over to their place and damn near bawl cried to them, so just being able to see them after a game, after a win, felt good," Manning said.

Years of hype built up the expectations surrounding the big, speedy quarterback with the famous last name who seemingly had all the attributes to excel at Texas.

Now Manning is reveling in his newfound existence on the opposite end of the spectrum.

"I think I kind of like being disregarded and counted out," Manning said.

articles.title: SEC Program Gets $500K Payback One Week After Its Own Field Storm vs. Alabama
articles.summary: Shane Beamer spent most of October answering questions about his future at South Carolina. Then the Gamecocks went to Gainesville on October 10 and beat then...
articles.body:
Shane Beamer spent most of October answering questions about his future at South Carolina. Then the Gamecocks went to Gainesville on October 10 and beat then-No. 16 Florida 38-19, ending an eight-game SEC losing streak. A bye week followed, and a ranked SEC visitor was waiting in Columbia. What unfolded gave Beamer a night to remember, but it also came with a costly catch.

South Carolina faces $500K SEC fine after Tennessee upset

South Carolina stunned No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 at Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday night. Malik Orsan's 48-yard field goal sailed through as time expired, and thousands of fans poured onto the field .

The South Carolina Gamecocks (4-3, 2-3 SEC) built a 14-0 lead, but Tennessee scored 21 points in the second quarter and later led 24-17. With 3:35 left, the Vols went for it on fourth-and-1 from the South Carolina 39 and were stopped.

Quarterback LaNorris Sellers made them pay. He fought through two defenders on third-and-goal, and the tying touchdown stood after review with 1:17 left. He ran for 96 yards and two scores.

Beamer praised Sellers. "He's freakin unbelievable," Beamer said afterword. "The play he made to score that touchdown. Unreal, one of the great plays probably in the history of South Carolina football."

Dylan Stewart then sacked George MacIntyre and forced a fumble with 33 seconds left. Tomiwa Durojaiye recovered at the Tennessee 34, setting up Orsan's winner.

Under the SEC's access-to-competition-area policy, every field storm now carries a flat $500,000 fine, paid to the visiting school. Tennessee paid the same amount a week earlier after its fans stormed the field following a win over Alabama. The league has not yet announced this penalty, but it is expected.

Now the spotlight shifts to Beamer, whose future looked far different three weeks ago.

Shane Beamer's job security was in doubt three weeks ago

Three weeks earlier, the mood around Beamer was bleak. South Carolina blew a 17-0 lead and lost 35-34 in overtime to Kentucky on October 3, extending its SEC losing streak to eight games. Fans voiced their anger, and buyout talk grew louder.

Asked about his standing, he pointed to the support he had been getting.

"I don't know anything other than what they've told me, that they've been super-supportive," Beamer told reporters. "And have been all along. Wish we could have put a better result on the field tonight."

A report suggested that, Beamer's job appeared safe before the Florida game , with a bye week viewed as a potential window for a coaching change. Instead, the Gamecocks won in Gainesville, took their bye, and beat ranked Tennessee at home.

Two straight wins over ranked opponents have changed the conversation, though questions about the long-term picture remain.

South Carolina improves to 4-3 and travels to Oklahoma on October 31. Tennessee falls to 6-2 and gets time off to regroup. Both teams will aim to carry the lessons of this college football thriller into November.

articles.title: Big 12 Coach Explains Why He Donated $2 Million to His Own Football Program
articles.summary: The Utah football coach and his wife, Liz, donated to the program, explaining their decision to give back to the university. The coach said the university ha...
articles.body:
The Utah football coach and his wife, Liz, donated to the program, explaining their decision to give back to the university.

The coach said the university had given a great deal to his family, which has longstanding ties to the institution. His father played football for Utah, he played safety for the Utes, and his wife also attended the university.

Family ties drive donation to support Utah Football's future

Utah Utes head coach Morgan Scalley has made it clear he wants to stay at the university . He and his wife, Liz, committed $2 million to the football program, a donation announced on March 12, 2026. During his October 23 appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, Scalley explained that the decision reflected his family's longstanding ties to the university and their desire to give back.

Morgan Scalley said the decision stemmed from his connection to the university. He grew up in Salt Lake City's Sugar House neighborhood, played safety for the Utes, and remains closely connected to the university

Explaining the family's reasons for making the donation, Scalley said : "Utah's done a ton for me and my family. My wife went here. My entire family went to the University of Utah. There's a lot the Utah family has given us. This is not a Morgan Scalley thing. I said that early on. It's about Utah football. It's about the University of Utah. When I'm gone, again, it'll still be Utah. We wanted to give back and help this community understand that we're in this together. I'm not going anywhere unless they kick me out of here."

Scalley said the contribution was intended to support Utah football and the wider university community rather than focus on him personally. He said the gift reflected the family's connection to the university

The donation comes during a period of significant change in college athletics, including NIL opportunities and revenue-sharing arrangements. These developments have reshaped the college football landscape. The $2 million gift is intended to support the Utah football program's long-term success, although the university has not specified how the money will be allocated.

Scalley has spent much of his coaching career with the program. He joined Utah as an administrative assistant in 2006, became a graduate assistant in 2007 and took over as safeties coach in 2008. From 2009 through 2015, he served as recruiting coordinator. He also assumed special teams responsibilities in 2015.

In 2016, Scalley became defensive coordinator and remained in the position through the 2025 season. The university appointed him head coach in December 2025, succeeding Kyle Whittingham.

During his first full season as head coach in 2026, Utah had a 6-0 record at the time of Scalley's October 23 appearance. The Utes had defeated Colorado 27-24 and were preparing for their next game against Houston Cougars .

The gift adds to Utah football's resources as the program continues under Scalley's leadership.

articles.title: Rams-Raiders takeaways: Sean McVay finally leans into run game
articles.summary: Sean McVay finally committed to the run game, calling 35 run plays to 29 pass plays
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams entered their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders needing a convincing performance to regain momentum, and the result offered plenty to evaluate on both sides of the football. From Stafford's command of the offense to the ground game's effectiveness and the defense's ability to control the Raiders in the first half, here are the biggest takeaways from the Rams' Week 7 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .

1st Down: Matthew Stafford is now Rams all time TD leader

Stafford's three touchdowns in the first half officially made him the all-time passing touchdown leader for the Rams franchise. Stafford's record breaking moment puts in a category of his own. He is now first all-time for both the Lions and Rams organizations.

His 156 touchdown passes surpassed Roman Gabriel, who played 11 years with the Rams from 1962-1972.

Through the first six weeks of the season, Los Angeles was throwing the ball about 65% of the time. The game plan was different this Sunday as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum were given 33 rushing attempts and worked that to the tune of 192 rushing yards. It was a huge effort to get the ground game going and make the LA offense multi-dimensional again.

The Rams trio of tight ends combined for 11 receptions, 82 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. Colby Parkinson led the group with 5 receptions and 48 yards. Davis Allen collected the first two touchdowns and nearly added a third. As for Higbee, he hauled in a huge third down conversion to prevent any thought of a Raiders comeback.

In the first half, the defense was stout. The interior defensive line was a stout despite being without Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Aaron Donald, Ty Hamilton, and Braden Fiske held the Raiders to 48 rushing yards on 17 rushing attempts (2.8 per attempt). The secondary forced multiple incompletions including three 4th down stops. Things got a little dicey because of some sloppiness on the offensive side and putting the defense in short fields. Despite being without 4 defensive starters, the Rams defense got the job done with a few backups like Shaun Dolac and Emmanuel Forbes being good enough in the win.

articles.title: Oregon Fires First-Year Offensive Coordinator Amid Disappointing Season
articles.summary: Oregon Ducks has fired its offensive coordinator following the team’s 21-10 loss to Illinois on October 24. The decision came after the Ducks struggled to pr...
articles.body:
Oregon Ducks has fired its offensive coordinator following the team's 21-10 loss to Illinois on October 24. The decision came after the Ducks struggled to produce points in three consecutive games.

Oregon's offense has scored no more than 17 points in each of those three games, with the Ducks losing to UCLA and Illinois while recording a win over Nebraska.

Oregon dismisses offensive coordinator after Illinois loss

Oregon has fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following its 21-10 loss to Illinois on Saturday. On3 reporter Pete Nakos reported the decision. The Ducks hold a 4-3 overall record and a 2-2 mark in Big Ten play.

Oregon produced 42 total points across its last three games. The Ducks lost to UCLA, defeated Nebraska and then fell to Illinois.

Against Illinois, Oregon led 10-0 at halftime but did not score again. Illinois scored 21 unanswered points to win 21-10. The Ducks finished with 426 total yards but converted just four of 15 third-down attempts.

After the loss, Nakos reported the move in a social media post, writing : "Oregon has dismissed offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer."

Quarterback Dylan Raiola completed 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards against Illinois. Running back Jordon Davison recorded 92 rushing yards, while Dierre Hill added 83. Wide receiver Dakorien Moore caught nine passes for 70 yards.

Oregon has also played without starting quarterback Dante Moore for three consecutive games. Moore suffered a concussion against USC, leaving Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas to handle quarterback duties during his absence.

Mehringer joined head coach Dan Lanning's staff in January 2022 as the team's tight ends coach. He later became co-offensive coordinator while continuing to coach tight ends. For the 2026 season, he took over as Oregon's full-time offensive coordinator after Will Stein left the program to become Kentucky's head coach.

During the 2025 season, when Mehringer served as co-offensive coordinator, Oregon averaged 36.9 points and 452.2 total yards per game.

Lanning announced Mehringer's departure in an official statement on October 25. He thanked Mehringer for his work with the program, acknowledged his contributions over several seasons and said he believed the offense needed a new direction.

Lanning said , "This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward."

Oregon has not announced who will replace Mehringer as offensive coordinator or take over offensive play-calling duties.

The Ducks are scheduled to host Northwestern at Autzen Stadium on October 31. Their remaining regular-season opponents also include Ohio State, Michigan, Michigan State and Washington.

images.caption: Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning, left, talks to Oregon Ducks offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer before the game as the Oregon Ducks host the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Oct. 17, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon.

articles.title: Brewers manager says of flight piloted by pitcher's uncle: 'I didn’t know Quinn threw a knuckleball'
articles.summary: (AP) — Pat Murphy was quick with a quip for the pilot crew of the charter flight that brought the Milwaukee Brewers to Florida on Sunday for World Series Gam...
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Pat Murphy was quick with a quip for the pilot crew of the charter flight that brought the Milwaukee Brewers to Florida on Sunday for World Series Game 3.

"Hey, thanks, guys. I didn't know Quinn threw a knuckleball," the Brewers manager said Sunday after the plane encountered a little turbulence.

GJ Priester, an uncle of Brewers pitcher Quinn Priester, was captain of the flight on a United Airlines Boeing 737. Alex Priester, a cousin of the right-hander, was first officer.

"Our flight was smooth as heck all flight and right when we came in, it really got a little knuckleballish," Murphy said, holding his right hand out and shaking it like a bouncing plane.

Murphy said the Brewers had five charter flights to bring all the family members and employees to the games at Tropicana Field. The Brewers held a 2-0 lead over the Tampa Bay Rays going into Game 3 of the best-of-seven series on Monday.

"The landing was a little rough," Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby said light-heartedly. "Certainly a cool thing. I guess we're in good hands."

GJ Priester was hired by United Airlines in 1995 and is a member of the family that founded Priester Aviation, which arranges charter flights.

Dwight Schmidt, father of New York Yankees pitcher Clarke Schmidt, piloted the team's family charter flights during the 2024 World Series .

Quinn Priester has not pitched for the Brewers since last year's NL Championship Series. The 26-year-old started the season on the injured list because of right thoracic outlet syndrome and made eight minor league injury rehabilitation appearances from April 22 through June 8.

He had season-ending surgery on June 22 with Dr. Gregory Pearl, who removed a rib to create space around nerves.

articles.title: USC football rumors: Trojans brass would ‘welcome’ Lincoln Riley pursuing Baylor job
articles.summary: With the USC football team losing to the Wisconsin Badgers on Saturday, 24-7, there is no denying that there is a conversation surrounding the job security o...
articles.body:
With the USC football team losing to the Wisconsin Badgers on Saturday, 24-7, there is no denying that there is a conversation surrounding the job security of head coach Lincoln Riley . While some fans could be demanding that USC football make a change from Riley, this college football insider could be signaling that the coach could trigger a move.

The latest from Bruce Feldman of The Athletic comes after the news of Dave Aranda being fired by the Baylor Bears, opening a big college football gig. Feldman would have Riley as the "biggest wild card in this season." Feldman would even say that if Riley were to be interested in the job, the Trojans "would welcome a move," adding that he's a Texas native.

"The 43-year-old has a sterling reputation as an offensive coach and for working with QBs. But his five-year run at USC has been so underwhelming, it's worth asking if he'd like to re-shuffle the deck. We're pretty confident USC brass would welcome a move like this if Riley is intrigued, especially after the Trojans got mauled this weekend at Wisconsin, where his team was held to minus 17 rushing yards and seven points — fewest ever by a Riley-coached team."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

More on the USC football team this season with Lincoln Riley

Despite the USC football program being 6-2 on the season, Feldman claims that the Trojans "hasn't beaten anything close to a ranked team this season." With some key games left, Feldman says that aside from Riley winning three of the final four games, "it feels like a stretch that he'll be able to do enough to convince" the brass at USC that he's the guy.

"The Trojans have games left against Ohio State, at Indiana, a dreadful Maryland team and at UCLA," Feldman wrote. "His buyout with USC is massive, somewhere around $70 million. Would he be tempted to move back to Texas — and the Big 12?"

Riley leads the Trojans against Ohio State on Saturday, as an unranked team beating the Buckeyes could give the fanbase and the school some confidence, though some may believe his exit is inevitable.

articles.title: Seahawks-Chiefs live discussion: Will another unbeaten team lose?
articles.summary: Can Patrick Mahomes get a win in Seattle?
articles.body:
The undefeated Kansas City Chiefs travel to Seattle to take on Sam Darnold and the Seahawks.

The Chiefs will be without WR1 and WR2. They'll also be without right tackle Jaylon Moore. The last place you want to be is short-handed against this Seahawks defense. We saw how they can prey on teams last year when the 49ers weren't at full strength.

But it's Patrick Mahomes, and you're asking for it by doubting him. It'll be a tall task to come away victorious in Seattle. We saw what it took for the 49ers to win. Will it end differently for the Chiefs?

Darnold has thrown an interception in three of the four games since he returned from injury. It would be news if Darnold didn't turn the ball over at this point. Darnold gets a Chiefs defense that is ninth in the NFL in interception percentage.

I see the Seahawks winning comfortably, 24-14, in an ugly game.

articles.title: Rodgers moves past Manning on all-time TD passing list as Steelers win 3rd straight
articles.summary: SAINT-DENIS, France (AP) — Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh’s 16-10 win over the New Orleans S...
articles.body:
SAINT-DENIS, France (AP) — Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh's 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in the NFL's first regular-season game in France.

Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and scrambled for a key first down late in fourth quarter as the Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game.

Linebacker Payton Wilson had a red zone interception of Tyler Shough in the third quarter and the Saints (2-5) couldn't recover. New Orleans rushed for just 18 yards.

With the Saints threatening on their opening drive of the second half, Wilson stepped in front of a short pass intended for Chris Olave. The Steelers got in field-goal position and Boswell was good from 39 yards for a 16-10 lead.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Bucky Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns, and Tampa Bay forced four turnovers as the Buccaneers hammered Carolina in Baker Mayfield's return.

Mayfield, who missed the previous three games with a dislocated right thumb, attempted just 11 passes and threw for 64 yards while wearing a protective glove on his right hand. That was more than enough for him to improve to 7-1 against the Panthers, including 6-1 since joining the Bucs (2-5).

Mayfield didn't need to do much because Tampa Bay's run game, defense and special teams dominated. The Bucs had 258 yards on the ground, with Sean Tucker adding a 46-yard touchdown run to put Tampa Bay up by 37.

Carolina's Bryce Young turned the ball over three times. Al-Quadin Muhammad had a strip-sack of Young that Calijah Kancey returned 32 yards for a touchdown.

BALTIMORE (AP) — Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half, and Cincinnati rebounded from a desultory first two quarters to beat Baltimore, handing the Ravens a second straight divisional loss with Lamar Jackson sidelined.

Baltimore (4-3) dominated the first half but led only 13-0 after settling for a couple of short field goals. Then the Ravens blew a double-digit second-half lead for the second straight week and 10th time since the start of the 2022 season.

The Bengals (4-2) were shut out in their second meeting with Baltimore last season, and were scoreless through two quarters this time before going 66 yards on the first drive after halftime, capped by Burrow's 6-yard TD pass to Mike Gesicki.

Baltimore, which held the ball for 22:20 in the first half, went three-and-out on its first possession of the second. Burrow's 13-yard scoring pass to Tee Higgins put Cincinnati ahead to stay.

MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Harrison Smith capped another dominant performance by Minnesota's defense with the game-sealing interception, and the Vikings overcame another sluggish start to stay unbeaten with a victory over spiraling Indianapolis.

Linebacker Blake Cashman led the onslaught of pressure on Daniel Jones all afternoon with 12 tackles, two sacks, four passes defensed and three quarterback hits for the Vikings (6-0), who won yet again despite minimal production from Kyler Murray and the offense.

Smith picked off Jones around midfield with about a minute left to kill the last-ditch drive by the Colts (2-5) before it ever got going, the 40th career interception for the stalwart safety who decided right before the regular season to return for his 15th year.

Jones went 13 for 122 for 108 yards and lost 44 yards on four sacks, with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores continually sending blitzers into the backfield.

Will Reichard made three field goals for the Vikings, including a 52-yarder with 1:39 left after his 59-yard try was blocked by Grover Stewart earlier in the fourth quarter.

ATLANTA (AP) — Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed San Francisco its first loss.

San Francisco (6-1) was already thin at wide receiver before its offense faced additional limitations when running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury.

Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted Brock Purdy's pass intended for Jordan Watkins with 2:34 remaining. It was Purdy's second interception. Daniels then recovered a fumble by George Kittle with less than a minute remaining.

The 49ers had only six turnovers in their first six games.

Penix threw scoring passes to tight ends Nick Muse and Kyle Pitts before giving Atlanta (3-4) a 26-14 lead with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Drake London in the fourth quarter. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with no interceptions.

EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score, leading Miami to its first win of the season with a victory over New York Jets.

The Dolphins (1-5) came off their bye-week break and avoided their first 0-6 start since 2019 by scoring on their first two drives and controlling most of the game before holding on to give coach Jeff Hafley his first win.

Trailing 28-17 with 4:44 left, the Jets (2-5) made a late push. On fourth-and-4, Geno Smith completed a short pass to Isaiah Davis, who zipped downfield 41 yards to the Dolphins 18. Three plays later, Smith found Mason Taylor in the back left corner of the end zone for a 12-yard touchdown, the tight end's second of the game.

Penalties negated New York's first two 2-point tries before Smith threw to Taylor to make it 28-25 with 3:24 left.

But Willis sealed the victory when he pushed forward for 2 yards on fourth-and-1 as the Dolphins celebrated and frustrated Jets fans filed out of MetLife Stadium.

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Deshaun Watson led his fifth game-winning drive in the fourth quarter this season, connecting with Harold Fannin Jr. on a 36-yard catch-and run that set up Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired, and Cleveland beat Tennessee for its fifth win in six games.

Watson ran for a touchdown and threw for 308 yards. Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards in his best game yet.

The AFC North-leading Browns (5-2) had two takeaways as they started a three-game road swing with a win.

Szmyt got the chance with his game-winning kick to make up for clanking a 43-yarder off the right upright within the first minute of the fourth quarter. The Titans responded with a drive capped by a 29-yard field goal by Joey Slye, which tied the game at 17-all with 8:41 remaining.

HOUSTON (AP) — Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run in overtime lifted New York to a win over Houston.

Cam Skattebo had a 16-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter and his 42-yard scamper to set up Singletary's game-winning run. He had 17 carries for 124 yards after not having a carry last Sunday following a costly fumble two weeks ago.

J.J. McCarthy moved the ball effectively for the Giants (4-2-1) in his first start of the season after coach John Harbaugh benched Jameis Winston. He was 20 of 28 for 252 yards in the stadium in which he won the national title with Michigan in January 2024.

The Texans (2-5) got the ball first in overtime, but New York's defense forced a three-and-out with Kayvon Thibodeaux dropping a potential interception on second down.

GLENDALE, Ariz. (AP) — Bo Nix ran for a 62-yard touchdown , RJ Harvey turned a short screen pass into a 52-yard touchdown and Denver used a handful of big offensive plays to beat Arizona.

The Cardinals have lost 10 straight home games in a streak that's lasted 406 days.

The Broncos (5-2) have struggled on offense for most of this season and that trend continued for part of Sunday's game, but Nix and Harvey took advantage of costly mistakes by the Cardinals' defense to get things moving.

Denver has won three straight. Its defense was dominant once again with 12 quarterback hits, six tackles for a loss and three sacks.

Nix's long touchdown run came late in the second quarter, giving the Broncos a 13-6 lead. He dropped back to pass and then stepped up in pocket, surging forward when a huge patch of grass appeared. No one on the Cardinals' defense was near him until a few yards before the end zone, when he sidestepped a tackle and tumbled forward for the touchdown.

Denver extended its lead to 20-6 midway through the third quarter when Harvey caught a short screen pass, took advantage of plenty of blocking and ran untouched to the end zone.

Nix finished 15 of 29 passing for 222 yards. He also had 73 yards rushing.

DETROIT (AP) — Jake Bates made a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give Detroit a win over Green Bay.

The Lions (4-2) have won two straight for the first time this season, putting them in third place in the NFC North behind Minnesota (6-0) and Chicago (5-2).

The Packers (4-3) had a three-game winning streak stopped and dropped to last place in the NFC North, likely lamenting a lot of penalties that went against them. The AFC North also has all four teams with winning records.

Detroit coach Dan Campbell, who is known for being aggressive, seemed to make a reckless decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his 24 with just under 5 minutes to play. Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for no gain, but the curious choice didn't backfire.

One play after Jordan Love put a pass on Josh Jacobs' hands for an incompletion that landed in in the end zone, rookie Trey Smack missed a 35-yard field goal after D.J. Wonnum got a finger on the kick. Smack missed from 26 in the first half.

With a chance to drive for a winning score, Goff connected with Sam LaPorta on an 18 -yard pass and Karl Brooks was called for a late hit on the quarterback gave Detroit the ball at the Green Bay 45.

LAS VEGAS (AP) — Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns to become the Rams' career leader in passing TDs, and Los Angeles resembled the team previously favored to win the Super Bowl, beating Las Vegas.

The Rams (3-4) still have a ways to go to overcome their slow start and numerous injuries, but this victory improves their chances to be a factor in the playoff race. Since the NFL playoffs expanded from 12 to 14 teams in 2020, 10 of 41 clubs have made the playoffs after opening 3-4, with just 4 of 33 making it after going 2-5.

Stafford has 155 touchdown passes in a Rams uniform, one more than previous team record holder Roman Gabriel.

Las Vegas native Puka Nacua, who had been listed as questionable with a calf injury, caught eight passes for 68 yards and a touchdown for the Rams, and tight end Davis Allen had two TD catches — his first trips to the end zone this season.

Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined to rush for 192 yards and two touchdowns for Los Angeles.

The Raiders' Kirk Cousins passed for 295 yards with touchdowns to Tre Tucker and running back Ashton Jeanty. Tucker finished with five receptions for 103 yards, and Jeanty hauled in eight catches for 61 yards. Cousins leads the NFL with 16 TD passes.

articles.title: Winners and Losers from the Vikings' Week 7 win over the Colts
articles.summary: Here are the winners and losers from the Vikings' Week 7 win over the Colts.
articles.body:
The theme for the Minnesota Vikings season has been "The defense will save us", and that rang true again today. The defense once again came to play, leading the charge en route to a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts . With the defense flying around and the offense showing its inconsistency once more, who are the winners and losers from today's game?

Jordan Mason returned from IR today and looked like he had even more pep in his step than before. Mason led the running back room today in touches and yards on the ground. Mason rushed for 68 yards on 15 carries, and looks to maintain control of the lead back role...so long as a certain Colts running back doesn't come to town soon.

Coincidence that the new Call of Duty release is in line with a poor Kyler Murray performance?

All joking aside, Murray struggled with accuracy today, throwing for just a 58% completion percentage on 24 attempts. Murray missed multiple open receivers and a handful of open reads. Murray has to be better going forward, more like the previous two weeks.

Cashman was everywhere on defense for the Vikings today, taking over as the leader today. This one is going to go down as one of, if not the best game of Cashman's career.

It's hard to imagine that Justin Jefferson isn't quietly frustrated behind the scenes. Just four receptions on seven targets today for Jefferson, and the passes coming his way were erratic and often off-target. Kevin O'Connell is an honorable mention for this selection, as the decision not to get Jefferson way more involved is certainly a decision.

articles.title: ‘There’s no way’: Tom Brady does not hold back on referees on Fox broadcast
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions beat the Green Bay Packers 20-17 on Sunday thanks to a Jake Bates field goal on the final play. But the officials played a big role in the...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions beat the Green Bay Packers 20-17 on Sunday thanks to a Jake Bates field goal on the final play. But the officials played a big role in the outcome, too, and analyst Tom Brady wasn't happy about it.

Calling the game for Fox, Brady repeatedly took issue with the penalties, including a roughing the passer call on the Packers that helped set up Detroit's game-winning drive.

The Lions improved to 4-2 with the win, while the Packers fell to 4-3. But several of the game's biggest moments came down to flags.

The Packers were hit with two questionable roughing the passer calls, including one on Karl Brooks during the Lions' final drive as Detroit then went 71 yards in 10 plays to set up the winning kick.

The Lions weren't spared, either. Before that drive, linebacker Derrick Barnes was flagged for a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty after a hit on Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd that gave Green Bay an automatic first down on a drive where they ultimately tied the game at 17.

Brady made it pretty clear that he didn't agree with the call on Barnes' hit.

After hearing that a flag was on the way, he responded, "There's no way," and when the penalty was announced, he added, "Come on, man."

"Oh, he's just turning his right shoulder away from it. That's allowed 99 out of 100," Brady said, via Awful Announcing .

"Yeah, it's a bang-bang play. I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you're on the field, you've got to pursue that ball," Brady continued. "If he catches it, he needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball off him as a pass defense. He can't go in there and put his hand on him."

Later in the fourth quarter, Brooks was flagged for roughing the passer for a hit against Jared Goff with 2:40 left, and Brady was even more frustrated.

"No, my goodness, what is that? There's no way," Brady said, via Awful Announcing . "That's definitely not roughing the passer. I mean, you just— you're just ripping through the line of scrimmage to try to get the quarterback on the ground. Look, I love Goff standing there in the pocket, but you just can't keep tacking on 15 yards."

Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino agreed with Brady.

"It wasn't late. They might have said head-neck area, but this is not head-neck area. His head is up. That's teach-tape tackle. That's not roughing the passer," Blandino said.

Play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt added that the call was "certainly not a penalty," and said of Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, "he's calm, but he's got to be losing it inside."

Needless to say, Packers fans probably felt the same way.

articles.title: What we learned about UConn women’s basketball in three exhibition games
articles.summary: UConn women’s basketball went 3-0 in the preseason. Here’s what we learned about Jovana Popovic, the defense, center play and injuries.
articles.body:
STORRS, CT — UConn couldn't have asked for a better way to end its preseason.

On Sunday, the Huskies defeated Army 86-50 to go undefeated in their three exhibition games. UConn also defeated Syracuse and Texas in blowout fashion, leaving no doubt that it is a contender for a national championship.

Through this three-game stretch, the Huskies have proven they have the potential to be an elite defensive team with a potent offense led by reigning national player of the year Sarah Strong.

While these games don't count, the Huskies have given a peek to what this team could look like going forward.

Here's what we learned about UConn after three exhibition game wins:

See photos of UConn women's basketball vs Army

Jovana Popovic has been even better than advertised.

The Serbian guard has been UConn's second leading scorer this preseason, showcasing her skills to be a shot creator and a spot-up shooter in the backcourt.

Her poise impressed coach Geno Auriemma the most. Teams have tried to pick her up full court, but she hasn't wilted through the pressure. She's turned the ball over just seven times across these three games.

Popovic has played off starting point guard KK Arnold well as she has proven she's just as much of a threat when she's off the ball. When she does get opportunities to create with the ball in her hands, she's been outstanding as a guard who can shoot off the bounce or get to the rim with her strength and quickness.

When forward Blanca Quiñonez returns from her shoulder recovery, she almost certainly will be a starter. But Popovic's spot should be safe after showing she could be one of the top guards in the country this season.

Defense was perhaps UConn's biggest strength in preseason play.

The Huskies held all three of their opponents to 61 points or less with a defense that got better in the second half.

UConn forced turnovers at a high rate, averaging 18 takeaways. Teams have shot an average of 36.77% from the field and 26.69% from the 3-point line.

"I think that we have emphasized a lot on pressuring the ball," sophomore guard Allie Ziebell said. "I think getting in those gaps and taking some things away will really disrupt other teams that we play against."

Still searching for consistent center play

With Strong becoming more perimeter oriented, UConn will almost always have a traditional center on the floor.

Jana El Alfy has gotten the starting nod but has split time with freshman Olivia Vukosa. Auriemma said he's still figuring out how to play both of them next to Strong.

"The fact that Sarah is spending a lot of time on the perimeter, which I like, that leaves a lot of room for those big guys to work," Auriemma said. "But we got to make sure they don't get in the way."

The Huskies aren't even fully healthy yet, but they already have multiple players on the bench that can come in and contribute.

Ziebell has shown that she could be a reliable shooter in the second unit, hitting 3-of-7 shots from beyond the arc against Army.

Kayleigh Heckel has slotted in as the backup point guard this preseason, and Auriemma has said there could be opportunities to find her own shot within the offense this year.

Vukosa is almost certainly going to be the backup center going forward. While she is still adjusting to the college game, her passing and her presence on the offensive glass will make her an important piece to the frontcourt's rotation.

Will the injured players be ready for the season opener?

Three of UConn's players are still questionable to play in next week's opener against Cornell.

Blanca Quiñonez (shoulder) and Marine Dursus (foot) have not seen any action during UConn's three exhibition games. Morgan Cheli (undisclosed) played in UConn's first preseason game against Syracuse but has been absent ever since.

Auriemma said all three players are in "ready-to-play" protocol and all have the possibility to suit up for the opener.

"I've kind of stopped asking because I keep getting the same answer," Auriemma said when asked about the status of his three players.

articles.title: Big 12 football standings, results after Week 8 of 2026 season
articles.summary: Utah is the only undefeated team in the Big 12 after BYU and Texas Tech fell to unranked teams. Here is a look at the full Big 12 standings.
articles.body:
The Big 12 had a chaotic weekend. It started with Cincinnati outplaying Texas Tech, who won just their second conference game of the season. BYU also fell in one of the wildest games you will ever see, with a blocked field goal to end regulation and multiple penalties by the Cougars that kept UCF alive.

For a while, it looked like Utah might join the chaos after narrowly escaping last week with a win over Colorado . However, they fought back in the second half to become the only undefeated team left in the Big 12 and dropped Houston to two conference losses, effectively eliminating their chances of making the Big 12 championship.

Here is how the Big 12 standings look after Week 8.

articles.body:
Watching this game live, I thought the charts would look one of two ways coming out of this contest:

Glass half empty: "Alabama was lucky to grab those early turnovers and stay in this game" … Texas A&M's SR and XR would suggest that they should've won this game

Glass half full: Or, that struggles always feel worse when watching live, and that Alabama was doing better — in terms of efficiency and explosiveness — than the scoreboard suggested.

And the "overall average performance" chart looks an awful lot like "Glass half full":

And, look, the game of football is four quarters, so we don't throw out insights just because they were of the "better late than never" variety … but the Tide pulled away there at the very end in a game where A&M was going toe to toe with them on efficiency.*

So, yes elements of this analysis do suggest some of that "Glass half empty" point of view. But then the fourth quarter happened, which we should just zoom in on.

* Though the explosiveness gap still very much exists in this chart, and in fact shows that Alabama was sticking around using a "boom and bust" offense — likely at least somewhat unintentionally — and posting >20% Explosiveness Rates in much of the first half. That's at least how we got a FG and another TD in the first half. This was all while A&M was mostly hanging in the <10% (very low) end of the XR range.

But what the heck happened in that 4th quarter ? Texas A&M went from a stubborn competitor to being completely pantsed in a matter of plays, mustering exactly one successful play (a pass) and zero explosive plays in the 4th quarter.

And for their part, Keelon and co. suddenly decided to add ~50% to their efficiencies and actually string some plays together. This quickly started looking like numbers you'd see in a cupcake game.

I'm not an X's and O's analyst, but I do have some theories as to what flipped the switch for Alabama:

At the 4th quarter mark, an ancient curse was finally lifted (maybe something from DeBoer's mysterious past in the remote North).

Keelon found a magic Mario mushroom in the medical tent.

Grubb logged into RBR to get suggestions from the game thread.

Alabama DL Fatutoa Henry is actually a minor deity that grants +10 strength to allies in his immediate area. (Good thing we put him in).

Maybe it was the Moon? I think it rose right around 5pm local yesterday.

I'm sure CrimsonHayate will be along in the comments to confirm which of the above was actually happening out there (after he gets the all-22 view, of course).

Yes, yesterday's game was a rich chapter in the long tale of Alabama's running game. And no, it wasn't the chapter where our intrepid heroes finally reach enlightenment …

I think there's solid rationale conjectured around these parts as to what happened in to the running game in this one — injured OL, a good DL — but it does seem by now that Grubb leans on the pass whenever things get uncomfortable. (I know this is the advanced analysis you show up for).

Once things did get comfortable — again, in the 4th quarter, I believe right when the Moon rose over the stadium walls — Grubb was happy to run the ball again, now with a lead. Funny enough, it still didn't really work until just about the very end of the game , which you might suspect was more about the Aggies giving up more than anything else.

I know we've all heard of "running to open up the passing game," but we might just be in an offensive system that tends to think of it the other way.

I mean, wow Uncle Rico. You can really play ball.

It made sense to think of Lotzier Brooks as the "next man up" after Ryan Coleman-Williams went down with injury — can he come back yet, please? — but it seems like Rico Scott has filled the gap more than anyone. It wasn't exactly our best day on offense out there, but Rico pulled in 6 successful catches, with 4 of those being explosive. That's a big day!

The Tight Ends really got in on the action this week, too, with 6 successful catches (of 7 total), including 2 explosvies across Josh Ford and Kaleb Edwards . Marshall Pritchett also followed his new trend of being Keelon's late-game safety blanket in the flats.

All in all, this chart shows some good spread for a game that "wasn't going well" for most of it.

I was wondering why this rushers chart felt weird, and it's because there are no explosive rushes on it. Like, not even one. (Very 2025 coded, though even then we'd usually see at least one).

But Daniel Hill showed that he's not just going away because we've got talented freshman. Trae'shawn Brown struggled to get going in this one, with just 1/7 successful rushes (14.3% rushing SR); but Hill led the pack and managed a respectable 44.4% Rushing SR of his own (plus those two successful passes caught, too).

And we're on to the bye week … which couldn't come at a better time. I mean listen, some of us have to graph things every week and the injuries are piling up at home.

I posted in the Feed earlier about the AP Poll and SP+ numbers. And while I'm trying to enjoy this victory for 24 hours — plus other fun action across College ball yesterday! — it's hard not to see LSU absolutely lurking in the stats while they wait for us to come to town in two weeks.

But that's football in the SEC, baby. Just (please) win.

articles.title: Sean Payton: Reverse that led to Jaylen Waddle injury was an "awful" play call
articles.summary: Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a chest injury on a fourth quarter play that head coach Sean Pay...
articles.body:
Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a chest injury on a fourth quarter play that head coach Sean Payton would like to have back.

Payton tried to get the ball to Waddle on a reverse that saw quarterback Bo Nix flip the ball to the wideout in the backfield. Waddle couldn't handle the flip and stayed down after jumping on the ball to avoid a turnover. Waddle did not return to the 30-16 win and Payton chastised himself for the call without being asked about it in his postgame press conference.

Payton didn't offer a detailed update on Waddle's condition and it will be something to monitor as they move toward their Week 8 date with the Chiefs.
